title.raw: 卷一百八十 列傳第一百零五 李德裕 Volume 180 Biographies 105: Li Deyu

sentences.zh: 李德裕李德裕，字文饒，元和宰相吉甫子也。

translations.literal: Li Deyu—Li Deyu, styled Wenrao, was the son of Jifu, chief minister in the Yuanhe reign.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu, styled Wenrao, was the son of Li Jifu, who had served as chief minister under Emperor Xianzong.

sentences.zh: 少力於學，既冠，卓犖有大節。

translations.literal: In youth he applied himself to study; after coming of age, he was outstanding and possessed great integrity.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he devoted himself to learning, and once he came of age he proved outstanding, with a strong sense of public duty.

sentences.zh: 不喜與諸生試有司，以廕補校書郎。

translations.literal: He did not care to compete with other students in the examinations of the authorities, and entered office by yin privilege as proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: He declined to sit for the civil examinations alongside other students and instead entered service through hereditary privilege as a proofreader in the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 河東張弘靖辟為掌書記。

translations.literal: Zhang Hongjing of Hedong recruited him as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hongjing, military governor of Hedong, took him on as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 府罷，召拜監察御史。

translations.literal: When the prefectural office was abolished, he was summoned and appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: When that command ended, he was summoned to the capital and appointed an investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，擢翰林學士。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong took the throne, he was promoted to Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong ascended the throne, Li Deyu was promoted to Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 帝為太子時，已聞吉甫名，由是顧德裕厚，凡號令大典冊，皆更其手。

translations.literal: When the emperor had been crown prince he had already heard Jifu's name; for this reason he favored Deyu generously, and all edicts and great documents passed through his hand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already known Li Jifu by reputation when he was still crown prince, and therefore treated Deyu with exceptional favor: every major edict and state document was drafted in his hand.

sentences.zh: 數召見，賚獎優華。

translations.literal: He was summoned repeatedly and rewarded with lavish gifts and honors.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned him often and heaped gifts and honors upon him.

sentences.zh: 帝怠荒於政，故戚裏多所請丐，挾宦人詗禁中語，關托大臣。

translations.literal: The emperor was negligent and dissolute in government, so imperial kin made many requests, using eunuchs to spy on palace talk and press ministers through connections.
translations.idiomatic: Because the emperor neglected government, members of the imperial clan pressed many requests, using eunuchs to eavesdrop on palace affairs and lobby senior ministers through back channels.

sentences.zh: 德裕建言：「舊制，駙馬都尉與要官禁不往來。

translations.literal: Deyu submitted advice: "By old regulation, commandants-escort and important officials were forbidden to associate.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu advised: "Under the old rules, commandants-escort and high officials were forbidden to mingle.

sentences.zh: 開元中，訶督尤切，今乃公至宰相及大臣私第。

translations.literal: In the Kaiyuan era prohibition and supervision were especially strict; now they openly go to the private residences of chief ministers and great officials.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign enforcement had been especially strict, yet now they openly visit the private homes of chief ministers and other senior officials.

sentences.zh: 是等無佗材，直洩漏禁密，交通中外耳。

translations.literal: Such men have no other talent—they simply leak forbidden secrets and traffic between inside and outside.
translations.idiomatic: These men have no other ability; they merely leak palace secrets and shuttle influence between the court and the outside world.

sentences.zh: 請白事宰相者，聽至中書，無輒詣第。

translations.literal: I ask that those who report business to the chief minister be allowed only to come to the Secretariat, and not casually go to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: Let those who wish to report to the chief minister come only to the Secretariat, and not call at his private residence at will.

sentences.zh: 」帝然之。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 再進中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Secretariat drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted again, to Secretariat drafter.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授御史中丞。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was appointed vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 始，吉甫相憲宗，牛僧孺、李宗閔對直言策，痛詆當路，條失政。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Jifu was chief minister under Emperor Xianzong, Niu Sengru and Li Zongmin answered the direct-criticism policy examination, bitterly denouncing those in power and listing failures of government.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Jifu served Emperor Xianzong as chief minister, Niu Sengru and Li Zongmin took the "direct criticism" policy examination and sharply attacked those in power, itemizing governmental failures.

sentences.zh: 吉甫訴於帝，且泣，有司皆得罪，遂與為怨。

translations.literal: Jifu appealed to the emperor and wept; the examining officials were all punished, and thus a feud was formed.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu appealed to the emperor in tears; the examiners were all punished, and from that time he and they were enemies.

sentences.zh: 吉甫又為帝謀討兩河叛將，李逢吉沮解其言，功未既而吉甫卒，裴度實繼之。

translations.literal: Jifu also planned for the emperor to campaign against the rebel generals of the two He regions; Li Fengji obstructed and dissolved his proposals. Before the achievement was complete Jifu died, and Pei Du in fact succeeded him.
translations.idiomatic: Jifu also urged the emperor to suppress the rebel generals of the two He regions, but Li Fengji blocked and undermined his plans. Jifu died before the campaign was finished, and Pei Du in fact took his place.

sentences.zh: 逢吉以議不合罷去，故追銜吉甫而怨度，擯德裕不得進。

translations.literal: Fengji was dismissed because his views did not agree; he therefore bore a grudge against Jifu and resented Du, and kept Deyu from advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji had been removed from office when his views clashed with others', and he still nursed a grievance against Jifu while resenting Pei Du; he blocked Deyu's advancement.

sentences.zh: 至是，間帝暗庸，訁木度使與元稹相怨，奪其宰相而己代之。

translations.literal: At this time, taking advantage of the emperor's dullness and mediocrity, he slandered Du so that Du and Yuan Zhen became mutually hostile, removed Du from the chief ministership, and replaced him himself.
translations.idiomatic: Now, exploiting the emperor's dullness and mediocrity, he slandered Pei Du until Du and Yuan Zhen were at odds, stripped Du of the chief ministership, and took the post himself.

sentences.zh: 欲引僧孺益樹黨，乃出德裕為浙西觀察使。

translations.literal: Wishing to draw Sengru in to strengthen his faction, he sent Deyu out as military governor of Zhexi.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking to bring Sengru in and build his faction further, he had Deyu posted out as military governor of Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 俄而僧孺入相，由是牛、李之憾結矣。

translations.literal: Before long Sengru entered the chief ministership, and from this the grievance between the Niu and Li factions was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Sengru entered the chief ministership, and from that point the feud between the Niu and Li factions was sealed.

sentences.zh: 初，潤州承王國清亂，竇易直傾府庫賚軍，貲用空殫，而下益驕。

translations.literal: At first Runzhou, following Wang Guoqing's rebellion, had seen Dou Yizhi empty the treasury to reward the army; funds were exhausted and the subordinates grew more arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Runzhou had lately suffered Wang Guoqing's rebellion; Dou Yizhi had emptied the treasury paying off the troops, leaving nothing in the coffers while the men below grew ever more arrogant.

sentences.zh: 德裕自檢約，以留州財贍兵，雖儉而均，故士無怨。

translations.literal: Deyu himself was frugal and disciplined, using retained prefectural funds to support the troops; though austere it was equitable, so the soldiers had no complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu practiced strict economy himself, using what the prefecture retained to support the troops; though supplies were lean, distribution was fair, and the men did not complain.

sentences.zh: 再期，則賦物儲牣。

translations.literal: After two terms, taxes and stores were full.
translations.idiomatic: Within two terms of office, tax revenues and storehouses were full again.

sentences.zh: 南方信禨巫，雖父母癘疾，子棄不敢養。

translations.literal: The south believed in pestilence shamans; even when parents had epidemic illness, sons abandoned them and dared not care for them.
translations.idiomatic: In the south people trusted shamans of pestilence; even when parents fell ill with contagious disease, sons would abandon them rather than nurse them.

sentences.zh: 德裕擇長老可語者，諭以孝慈大倫，患難相收不可棄之義，使歸相曉敕，違約者顯置以法。

translations.literal: Deyu selected elders who could be reasoned with, instructed them in the great norms of filial piety and kindness and the principle that in hardship one must receive one another and may not abandon kin, and had them return to teach one another; violators were openly punished by law.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu chose respected elders who could be reasoned with, taught them the duties of filial piety and mutual support in hardship, and sent them home to spread the message; offenders were openly punished under the law.

sentences.zh: 數年，惡俗大變。

translations.literal: Within several years the evil custom changed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the vicious custom was largely transformed.

sentences.zh: 又按屬州非經祠者，毀千餘所，撤私邑山房千四百舍，寇無所廋蔽。

translations.literal: He also investigated subordinate prefectures and destroyed more than a thousand shrines not authorized by canonical rites, and removed fourteen hundred private mountain lodges in the districts, so bandits had nowhere to hide.
translations.idiomatic: He also inspected the subordinate prefectures, tearing down more than a thousand unauthorized shrines and removing fourteen hundred private mountain lodges, so bandits had nowhere to conceal themselves.

sentences.zh: 天子下詔褒揚。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven issued an edict praising him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict commending him.

sentences.zh: 敬宗立，侈用無度，詔浙西上脂朅妝具，德裕奏：「比年旱災，物力未完。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jingzong took the throne, extravagant spending knew no limit; he ordered Zhexi to submit cosmetic and grooming articles. Deyu memorialized: "In recent years there have been drought disasters and material resources are not restored.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Jingzong came to the throne his spending was boundless; he ordered Zhexi to send cosmetic and grooming supplies. Deyu memorialized: "Droughts in recent years have left the region's resources unrecovered.

sentences.zh: 乃三月壬子赦令，常貢之外，悉罷進獻。

translations.literal: Moreover the amnesty of the third month on the renzi day abolished all tribute beyond regular levies.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty's amnesty of the third month, on the day renzi, abolished all presents beyond the regular tribute.

sentences.zh: 此陛下恐聚斂之吏緣以成奸，雕窶之人不勝其敝也。

translations.literal: This was because Your Majesty feared that revenue-gathering officials would use it to commit fraud, and that the carved-out and impoverished people could not bear the harm.
translations.idiomatic: That was because Your Majesty feared that revenue officers would use the opportunity for extortion, and that an already exhausted populace could not endure further exactions.

sentences.zh: 本道素號富饒，更李錡、薛蘋，皆榷酒於民，供有羨財。

translations.literal: This circuit has long been called rich; under Li Qi and Xue Ping both monopolized wine from the people and supplied surplus funds.
translations.idiomatic: This circuit has long been considered wealthy, yet under Li Qi and Xue Ping both had monopolized wine for the people and still produced surplus revenue.

sentences.zh: 元和詔書停榷酤，又赦令禁諸州羨餘無送使。

translations.literal: The Yuanhe edict stopped the wine monopoly, and an amnesty forbade prefectures to send surplus funds to the transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: An edict in the Yuanhe era ended the wine monopoly, and an amnesty forbade prefectures to forward surplus funds to the transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 今存者惟留使錢五十萬緡，率歲經費常少十三萬，軍用褊急。

translations.literal: What remains now is only fifty thousand strings of retained commissioner funds; annual routine expenses on average fall short by one hundred thirty thousand, and military supplies are strained.
translations.idiomatic: All that remains is fifty thousand strings in retained commissioner funds; routine annual expenses typically run one hundred thirty thousand short, and military supplies are desperately tight.

sentences.zh: 今所須脂朅妝具，度用銀二萬三千兩，金百三十兩，物非土產，雖力營索，尚恐不逮。

translations.literal: The cosmetic articles now required are estimated at twenty-three thousand taels of silver and one hundred thirty taels of gold; they are not local products, and even with strenuous procurement I fear we cannot meet the demand.
translations.idiomatic: The cosmetics now demanded would cost an estimated twenty-three thousand taels of silver and one hundred thirty taels of gold; they are not local products, and even with every effort at procurement I fear we cannot supply them.

sentences.zh: 願詔宰相議，何以俾臣不違詔旨，不乏軍興，不疲人，不斂怨，則前敕後詔，鹹可遵承。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to order the chief ministers to discuss how to enable me not to violate the edict, not to lack military provisions, not to weary the people, and not to gather resentment—then earlier and later edicts may all be followed.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty order the chief ministers to decide how I may obey the edict without starving military needs, exhausting the people, or provoking resentment, so that both your earlier and later orders can be honored.

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: " There was no reply.
translations.idiomatic: " He received no answer.

sentences.zh: 方是時，罷進獻，不閱月，而求貢使者足相接于道，故德裕推一以諷它。

translations.literal: At that time, though tribute presentations had been abolished, within less than a month envoys seeking to present tribute crowded the roads one after another; therefore Deyu used one case to admonish the others.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, although presents to the court had been abolished, within a month envoys seeking to offer tribute lined the roads; Deyu used this one request to admonish the rest.

sentences.zh: 又詔索盤絛繚綾千匹，復奏言：「太宗時，使至涼州，見名鷹，諷李大亮獻之，大亮諫止，賜詔嘉歎。

translations.literal: Again an edict demanded a thousand bolts of patterned silk with coiled trim. He memorialized again: "In Emperor Taizong's time an envoy reached Liangzhou, saw a famous hawk, and hinted that Li Daliang should present it; Daliang remonstrated and stopped it, and was granted an edict of praise and sighing approval.
translations.idiomatic: The court then demanded a thousand bolts of patterned silk with coiled trim. He memorialized again: "Under Emperor Taizong, an envoy at Liangzhou saw a famous hawk and hinted that Li Daliang should present it; Daliang remonstrated and stopped the gift, and the emperor issued an edict praising him.

sentences.zh: 玄宗時，使者抵江南捕鵁鶄、翠鳥，汴州刺史倪若水言之，即見褒納。

translations.literal: In Emperor Xuanzong's time envoys reached Jiangnan to capture fish hawks and kingfishers; Bianzhou prefect Ni Ruoshui spoke of it and was immediately praised and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanzong, envoys went to Jiangnan to capture fish hawks and kingfishers; Bianzhou prefect Ni Ruoshui protested and was immediately rewarded.

sentences.zh: 皇甫詢織半臂、造琵琶捍撥、鏤牙筩於益州，蘇頲不奉詔，帝不加罪。

translations.literal: Huangfu Xun wove half-sleeves, made pipa plectrums, and carved ivory tubes in Yizhou; Su Ting did not obey the edict, and the emperor did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: When Huangfu Xun wove half-sleeves, made pipa plectrums, and carved ivory tubes in Yizhou, Su Ting refused the order and the emperor did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 夫鵁鶄、鏤牙，微物也。

translations.literal: Fish hawks and carved ivory are trifling things.
translations.idiomatic: Fish hawks and carved ivory are trifling things.

sentences.zh: 二三臣尚以勞人損德為言，豈二祖有臣如此，今獨無之？

translations.literal: Yet two or three ministers still spoke of burdening the people and harming virtue—did the two founding emperors have such ministers while today alone has none?
translations.idiomatic: Yet two or three ministers still protested that such demands burdened the people and harmed the ruler's virtue—did the two founding emperors have such ministers while today we have none?

sentences.zh: 蓋有位者蔽而不聞，非陛下拒不納也。

translations.literal: Surely those in office screen and do not let you hear—not that Your Majesty refuses to accept.
translations.idiomatic: Surely those in high office shield you from such counsel—it is not that Your Majesty refuses to listen.

sentences.zh: 且立鵝天馬，盤絛掬豹，文彩怪麗，惟乘輿當禦。

translations.literal: Moreover standing-goose, heavenly horse, coiled trim, and leopard-cub patterns are bizarrely splendid in color and design—only the imperial carriage should use them.
translations.idiomatic: Patterns such as standing goose, heavenly horse, coiled trim, and leopard cub are extravagantly ornate—only the imperial carriage should bear them.

sentences.zh: 今廣用千匹，臣所未諭。

translations.literal: To use them widely in a thousand bolts—I do not understand.
translations.idiomatic: To demand a thousand bolts at once is something I cannot fathom.

sentences.zh: 昔漢文身衣弋綈，元帝罷輕纖服，故仁德慈儉，至今稱之。

translations.literal: Formerly Emperor Wen of Han wore coarse silk himself, and Emperor Yuan abolished light fine fabrics; therefore benevolence, virtue, kindness, and frugality are praised to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Han wore coarse silk, and Emperor Yuan abolished light fine fabrics; their benevolence and frugality are praised to this day.

sentences.zh: 願陛下師二祖容納，遠思漢家恭約，裁賜節減，則海隅蒼生畢受賜矣。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to take the two founding emperors as teachers in accepting remonstrance, reflect far on the Han house's respectful restraint, and grant a measured reduction—then all the people at the sea's edge would receive the gift.
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty follow the two founding emperors in welcoming remonstrance, recall the Han dynasty's restraint, and grant a reduction in the order—then every subject on the coast would benefit.

sentences.zh: 」優詔為停。

translations.literal: " A gracious edict halted it.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor issued a gracious edict and canceled the demand.

sentences.zh: 自元和後，天下禁毋私度僧。

translations.literal: From after the Yuanhe era the empire forbade private ordination of monks.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yuanhe era the empire forbade private ordination of monks.

sentences.zh: 徐州王智興紿言天子誕月，請築壇度人以資福，詔可。

translations.literal: Wang Zhixing of Xuzhou deceptively said it was the Son of Heaven's birth month and requested to build an altar to ordain people for merit and blessing; the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhixing of Xuzhou falsely claimed it was the emperor's birth month and asked to build an altar to ordain monks for merit; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 即顯募江淮間，民皆曹輩奔走，因牟擷其財以自入。

translations.literal: He immediately recruited openly between the Jiang and Huai; the people all rushed in crowds, and he seized their wealth for his own intake.
translations.idiomatic: He openly recruited across the Jiang-Huai region; people rushed in crowds while he extorted their money for himself.

sentences.zh: 德裕劾奏：「智興為壇泗州，募願度者，人輸錢二千，則不復勘詰，普加髡落。

translations.literal: Deyu impeached and memorialized: "Zhixing built an altar at Sizhou and recruited those wishing ordination; each person paid two thousand cash and was not examined further—all were universally tonsured.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu impeached him, reporting: "Zhixing built an altar at Sizhou and recruited volunteers for ordination; anyone who paid two thousand cash was tonsured without further inquiry.

sentences.zh: 自淮而右，戶三丁男，必一男剔發，規影傜賦，所度無算。

translations.literal: From the Huai westward, in households with three adult males one male was sure to be shaved, plotting to evade corvée and tax; those ordained were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: West of the Huai, in every household with three adult sons one was tonsured, aiming to escape corvée and tax obligations; the number ordained was beyond count.

sentences.zh: 臣閱度江者日數百，蘇、常齊民，十固八九，若不加禁遏，則前至誕月，江淮失丁男六十萬，不為細變。

translations.literal: I observe hundreds crossing the river daily to be ordained; among the common people of Su and Chang, eight or nine in ten—if not forbidden, by the birth month ahead the Jiang-Huai would lose six hundred thousand adult males; this is no small change.
translations.idiomatic: I see hundreds crossing the river each day to be ordained; in Suzhou and Changzhou eight or nine households in ten are affected. Unless this is stopped, by the birth month the Jiang-Huai region could lose six hundred thousand adult males—a grave matter.

sentences.zh: 」有詔徐州禁止。

translations.literal: " An edict ordered Xuzhou to forbid it.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict ordered Xuzhou to stop the practice.

sentences.zh: 時帝昏荒，數遊幸，狎比群小，聽朝簡忽。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor was benighted and dissolute, often went on excursions, was intimate with petty men, and was negligent in holding court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was benighted and dissolute, constantly traveling for pleasure, consorting with petty favorites, and neglecting court audiences.

sentences.zh: 德裕上《丹扆六箴》，表言：「'心乎愛矣，遐不謂矣'，此古之賢人篤于事君者也。

translations.literal: Deyu submitted the Six Admonitions at the Vermilion Screen, stating in a memorial: "'The heart loves—how could it be called distant?' This is how ancient worthies were devoted in serving their lord.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu submitted the Six Admonitions at the Vermilion Screen, writing: "'The heart loves—how could it be called distant?' That is how the ancients showed true devotion in serving their ruler.

sentences.zh: 夫跡疏而言親者危，地遠而意忠者忤。

translations.literal: One whose tracks are distant yet whose words are intimate is in peril; one whose post is far yet whose intent is loyal gives offense.
translations.idiomatic: Those distant in station who speak as intimates court danger; those far from court whose loyalty is sincere risk giving offense.

sentences.zh: 臣竊惟念拔自先聖，遍荷寵私，不能竭忠，是負靈鑒。

translations.literal: I privately reflect that I was raised by the former sage, have received favor everywhere, and if I cannot exhaust loyalty I fail the spiritual mirror.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that I was raised up by the late emperor, have received favor at every turn, and that failure to give my utmost loyalty would betray Heaven's clear sight.

sentences.zh: 臣在先朝，嘗獻《大明賦》以諷，頗蒙嘉采。

translations.literal: In the former court I once presented the Rhapsody on Great Brightness as admonition and received considerable commendation.
translations.idiomatic: In the previous reign I once presented the Rhapsody on Great Brightness as indirect remonstrance and was well received.

sentences.zh: 今日盡節明主，亦由是也。

translations.literal: Today in exhausting loyalty to the enlightened lord it is likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Today I serve the enlightened sovereign with the same full loyalty.

sentences.zh: 」其一曰《宵衣》，諷視朝希晚也；

translations.literal: " The first is Night Robes, admonishing tardiness in holding court;
translations.idiomatic: " The first, Night Robes, admonishes delaying court audiences;

sentences.zh: 二曰《正服》，諷服禦非法也；

translations.literal: the second is Correct Garments, admonishing unlawful imperial dress;
translations.idiomatic: the second, Correct Garments, admonishes improper dress at court;

sentences.zh: 三曰《罷獻》，諷斂求怪珍也；

translations.literal: the third is Cease Presentations, admonishing gathering strange treasures;
translations.idiomatic: the third, Cease Presentations, admonishes demanding exotic tribute;

sentences.zh: 四曰《納誨》，諷侮棄忠言也；

translations.literal: the fourth is Accept Admonition, admonishing scorning and abandoning loyal words;
translations.idiomatic: the fourth, Accept Admonition, admonishes rejecting loyal counsel;

sentences.zh: 五曰《辨邪》，諷任群小也；

translations.literal: the fifth is Discern Evil, admonishing employing petty men;
translations.idiomatic: the fifth, Discern Evil, admonishes trusting petty favorites;

sentences.zh: 六曰《防微》，諷偽遊輕出也。

translations.literal: the sixth is Guard against the Slight, admonishing disguised excursions and casual departures.
translations.idiomatic: the sixth, Guard against the Slight, admonishes secret outings and careless departures from the palace.

sentences.zh: 辭皆明直婉切。

translations.literal: The language throughout was clear, direct, and tactfully pointed.
translations.idiomatic: The wording throughout was clear, forthright, and tactfully pointed.

sentences.zh: 帝雖不能用其言，猶敕韋處厚諄諄作詔，厚謝其意。

translations.literal: Though the emperor could not use his words, he still ordered Wei Chuhou earnestly to draft an edict and thanked him warmly for his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Though the emperor did not follow his advice, he still had Wei Chuhou draft an edict of earnest thanks for his concern.

sentences.zh: 然為逢吉排笮，訖不內徙。

translations.literal: Yet because Fengji squeezed him out, he was never transferred inward to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Fengji blocked him, and he was never recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 時亳州浮屠詭言水可愈疾，號曰「聖水」，轉相流聞，南方之人，率十戶僦一人使往汲。

translations.literal: At that time a Bozhou monk falsely claimed water could cure illness and called it "holy water"; the report spread in turn, and southerners on average hired one man per ten households to go draw it.
translations.idiomatic: A monk in Bozhou falsely claimed that certain water could cure illness and called it "holy water"; the rumor spread, and in the south roughly one man in ten households was hired to fetch it.

sentences.zh: 既行若飲，病者不敢近葷血，危老之人率多死。

translations.literal: Once they went or drank it, the sick dared not approach meat or blood; the critically ill and elderly mostly died.
translations.idiomatic: After traveling or drinking it, the sick avoided meat and blood; many of the critically ill and elderly died.

sentences.zh: 而水鬥三十千，取者益它汲，轉鬻於道，互相欺訹，往者日數十百人。

translations.literal: Yet a dipper of water cost thirty thousand cash; fetchers drew more elsewhere, resold it along the road, cheated one another, and daily hundreds went.
translations.idiomatic: A dipper sold for thirty thousand cash; carriers drew more water elsewhere and resold it along the roads, cheating one another, while scores set out each day.

sentences.zh: 德裕嚴勒津邏捕絕之，且言：「昔吳有聖水，宋、齊有聖火，皆本妖祥，古人所禁。

translations.literal: Deyu strictly ordered ferry guards and patrols to cut it off, and said: "Formerly Wu had holy water, Song and Qi had holy fire—all rooted in prodigies and omens forbidden by the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu strictly ordered ferry guards and patrols to suppress it, reporting: "Wu once had 'holy water,' Song and Qi had 'holy fire'—all omens of mischief that the ancients forbade.

sentences.zh: 請下觀察使令狐楚填塞，以絕妄源。

translations.literal: I ask that an order go to the observation commissioner Linghu Chu to fill and block it, to cut off the source of delusion.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that observation commissioner Linghu Chu be ordered to seal the spring and cut off the source of this delusion.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: " The request was followed.
translations.idiomatic: " The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 帝方惑佛老，禱福祈年，浮屠方士，並出入禁中。

translations.literal: The emperor was then deluded by Buddhism and Daoism, praying for blessing and a good year; monks and alchemists alike came and went within the forbidden precincts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was then infatuated with Buddhism and Daoism, praying for blessings and good harvests, while monks and alchemists came and went within the palace.

sentences.zh: 狂人杜景先上言，其友周息元壽數百歲，帝遣宦者至浙西迎之，詔在所馳驛敦遣。

translations.literal: The madman Du Jingxian submitted that his friend Zhou Xiyuan was several hundred years old; the emperor sent eunuchs to Zhexi to welcome him, and edicts wherever he was ordered relay posts to urge him on.
translations.idiomatic: A crackpot named Du Jingxian reported that his friend Zhou Xiyuan was several hundred years old; the emperor sent eunuchs to Zhexi to escort him, with orders along the route to hurry him by relay post.

sentences.zh: 德裕上疏曰：「道之高者，莫若廣成、玄元；

translations.literal: Deyu submitted a memorial: "Of those lofty in the Way, none surpass Guangcheng and Xuanyuan;
translations.idiomatic: Deyu memorialized: "Of those supreme in the Way, none surpass Guangcheng and the Dark Primordial Lord;

sentences.zh: 人之聖者，莫若軒轅、孔子。

translations.literal: of those sage among men, none surpass Xuanyuan and Confucius.
translations.idiomatic: of those sage among men, none surpass the Yellow Emperor and Confucius.

sentences.zh: 昔軒轅問廣成子治身之要，曰：'無視無聽，抱神以靜，形將自正。

translations.literal: Formerly Xuanyuan asked Guangchengzi the essentials of governing the body; he said: 'Do not look, do not listen; embrace the spirit in stillness and the form will right itself.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago the Yellow Emperor asked Guangchengzi the secret of nurturing the body; he replied: 'Do not look, do not listen; hold the spirit in stillness and the body will right itself.

sentences.zh: 無勞子形，無搖子精，乃可長生。

translations.literal: Do not weary your form, do not shake your essence—only then may you live long.'
translations.idiomatic: Do not weary your body, do not disturb your essence—only then may you attain long life.'

sentences.zh: 慎守其一，以處其和。

translations.literal: Carefully guard the One and dwell in harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Guard the One carefully and dwell in harmony.

sentences.zh: 故我脩身千二百歲矣，形未嘗衰。

translations.literal: Therefore I have cultivated the body for twelve hundred years and my form has never declined.'
translations.idiomatic: Thus I have cultivated my body for twelve hundred years, and my form has never declined.'

sentences.zh: '又曰：'得吾道者上為皇，下為王。

translations.literal: ' He also said: 'One who obtains my Way may above be emperor, below be king.'
translations.idiomatic: ' He also said: 'Whoever attains my Way may be emperor above or king below.'

sentences.zh: '玄元語孔子曰：'去子之驕氣與多欲、態色與淫志，是皆無益於子之身。

translations.literal: ' Xuanyuan said to Confucius: 'Remove your arrogant air and many desires, your affected looks and licentious aims—all are of no benefit to your person.'
translations.idiomatic: ' The Dark Primordial Lord told Confucius: 'Cast off arrogance and excess desire, affectation and licentious ambition—all harm your person.'

sentences.zh: '陛下脩軒後之術，物色異人，若使廣成、玄元混跡而至，告陛下之言，亦無出於此。

translations.literal: ' Your Majesty cultivates the arts of Xuanyuan and the later sage and seeks strange men; if Guangcheng and Xuanyuan were to mingle among the crowd and come, what they would tell Your Majesty would not go beyond this.
translations.idiomatic: ' Your Majesty pursues the arts of the Yellow Emperor and the sages and seeks extraordinary men; yet if Guangcheng or the Dark Primordial Lord appeared in disguise, their counsel would be no different from this.

sentences.zh: 臣慮今所得者，皆迂怪之士，使物淖冰，以小術欺聰明，如文成、五利者也。

translations.literal: I fear those obtained now are all eccentric and bizarre men who muddy things like slush on ice, deceiving intelligence with petty arts, like Wencheng and Wuli.
translations.idiomatic: I fear those you will obtain are merely eccentric charlatans who muddy clear judgment with petty tricks, like the Wencheng and Wuli of old.

sentences.zh: 又前世天子雖好方士，未有禦其藥者。

translations.literal: Moreover, though former Sons of Heaven liked alchemists, none ever took their drugs.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, though earlier emperors favored alchemists, none ever took their elixirs.

sentences.zh: 故漢人稱黃金可成，以為飲食器則壽。

translations.literal: Therefore Han men said gold could be made and that using it for food and drink vessels would bring long life.
translations.idiomatic: Han writers said gold could be transmuted and that eating and drinking from golden vessels would grant long life.

sentences.zh: 高宗時劉道合、玄宗時孫甑生皆能作黃金，二祖不之服，豈非以宗廟為重乎？

translations.literal: In Gaozong's time Liu Daohe and in Xuanzong's time Sun Zaisheng could both make gold; the two founding emperors did not take it—was it not because they valued the ancestral temples?
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong, Liu Daohe, and under Xuanzong, Sun Zaisheng, could both make gold; neither emperor took their elixirs—was that not because they put the ancestral shrines first?

sentences.zh: 儻必致真隱，願止師保和之術，慎毋及藥，則九廟尉悅矣。

translations.literal: If you must summon true recluses, I wish you would stop at the arts of teacher, guardian, and harmony, and carefully not reach drugs—then the nine temples would be comforted and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: If you must summon genuine recluses, limit yourself to teachings of nurture and harmony, and do not touch elixirs—then the imperial ancestors would be reassured.

sentences.zh: 」息元果誕譎不情，自言與張果、葉靜能遊。

translations.literal: " Xiyuan proved extravagant, deceitful, and unnatural, claiming he associated with Zhang Guo and Ye Jingneng.
translations.idiomatic: " Xiyuan proved boastful and absurd, claiming friendship with Zhang Guo and Ye Jingneng.

sentences.zh: 帝詔畫工肖狀為圖以觀之，終帝世無它驗。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered painters to portray his likeness in a picture to view; through the emperor's reign there was no other verification.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered painters to depict him, but through that reign nothing further was proved.

sentences.zh: 文宗即位，乃逐之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong took the throne, he was expelled.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong came to the throne, he was driven out.

sentences.zh: 太和三年，召拜兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe he was summoned and appointed vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Taihe era he was summoned and appointed vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 裴度薦材堪宰相，而李宗閔以中人助，先秉政，且得君，出德裕為鄭滑節度使，引僧孺協力，罷度政事。

translations.literal: Pei Du recommended talent fit to be chief minister, but Li Zongmin with eunuch assistance held government first and had the ruler's favor; he sent Deyu out as military governor of Zheng-Hua, drew Sengru to cooperate, and removed Du from government affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du recommended men capable of serving as chief minister, but Li Zongmin, aided by eunuchs, seized power first and won the emperor's trust; he posted Deyu to Zheng-Hua, enlisted Niu Sengru's support, and stripped Pei Du of his governmental role.

sentences.zh: 二怨相濟，凡德裕所善，悉逐之。

translations.literal: The two grievances aided each other; all whom Deyu favored were entirely driven out.
translations.idiomatic: The two factions reinforced each other, and everyone Deyu favored was driven from office.

sentences.zh: 於是二人權震天下，黨人牢不可破矣。

translations.literal: Thus the two men's power shook the empire, and their faction members were firmly unbreakable.
translations.idiomatic: The two men's power now dominated the empire, and their factional bonds were unbreakable.

sentences.zh: 逾年，徙劍南西川。

translations.literal: After a year he was transferred to Western Chuan in Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was transferred to Western Chuan in Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 蜀自南詔入寇，敗杜元穎，而郭釗代之，病不能事，民失職，無聊生。

translations.literal: Shu, since Nanzhao invaded, had defeated Du Yuanying; Guo Zhao replaced him, was ill and unable to govern, the people lost their livelihoods, and had no means to live.
translations.idiomatic: Since Nanzhao's invasion had routed Du Yuanying, Guo Zhao replaced him but was too ill to govern; the people lost their livelihoods and could barely survive.

sentences.zh: 德裕至，則完殘奮怯，皆有條次。

translations.literal: When Deyu arrived, he restored the damaged, roused the timid—all had order and method.
translations.idiomatic: When Deyu arrived, he restored what was broken and roused the timid; everything was put in proper order.

sentences.zh: 成都既南失姚、協，西亡維、松，由清溪下沫水而左，盡為蠻有。

translations.literal: Chengdu had already lost Yao and Xie to the south and Wei and Song to the west; from Qingxi down the Moshui River to the left, all was held by the barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Chengdu had lost Yao and Xie to the south and Wei and Song to the west; everything from Qingxi down the Moshui and to the east was in barbarian hands.

sentences.zh: 始，韋皋招來南詔，復巂州，傾內資結蠻好，示以戰陣文法。

translations.literal: At the beginning Wei Gao had drawn Nanzhao in, recovered Xi prefecture, poured internal resources to bind barbarian friendship, and showed them battle formations and regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wei Gao had courted Nanzhao, recovered Xi prefecture, spent imperial resources to win their friendship, and taught them military formations and regulations.

sentences.zh: 德裕以皋啟戎資盜，其策非是，養成癰疽，第未決耳。

translations.literal: Deyu held that Gao had opened the frontier and armed robbers; his policy was wrong, nourishing an abscess that had only not yet burst.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu believed Gao had armed the frontier tribes at state expense; the policy was mistaken and had bred a boil that had not yet burst.

sentences.zh: 至元穎時，遇隙而發，故長驅深入，蹂剔千里，蕩無孑遺。

translations.literal: By Yuanying's time they seized an opening and erupted, therefore driving deep in a long campaign, trampling and plundering for a thousand li, sweeping until not one remained.
translations.idiomatic: By Du Yuanying's time they seized their chance and swept deep into the region, ravaging a thousand li until nothing was left standing.

sentences.zh: 今瘢夷尚新，非痛矯革，不能刷一方恥。

translations.literal: Now the scars from the barbarians are still fresh; without severe correction and reform, one cannot wash away a region's humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: The wounds inflicted by the barbarians were still raw; only drastic reform could erase the region's shame.

sentences.zh: 乃建籌邊樓，按南道山川險要與蠻相入者圖之左，西道與吐蕃接者圖之右。

translations.literal: He then built the Frontier Planning Tower; on the left he mapped the southern route's mountains and rivers where the terrain was strategically vital and where the barbarians could enter, and on the right the western route where it joined Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: He built a Frontier Planning Tower and charted it accordingly: on the left, the southern passes where barbarian raiders could enter; on the right, the western frontier where it met Tibetan territory.

sentences.zh: 其部落眾寡，饋餫遠邇，曲折鹹具。

translations.literal: The size of their tribes, the distance of supply routes near and far—all twists and turns were fully recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Tribal strengths, supply lines near and far, every bend in the terrain—all were mapped in full detail.

sentences.zh: 乃召習邊事者與之指畫商訂，凡虜之情偽盡知之。

translations.literal: He summoned those versed in frontier affairs to discuss and plan with him, and came to know all the enemy's true and false situations.
translations.idiomatic: He brought in frontier veterans to work through the maps with him until he knew every feint and stratagem the enemy might use.

sentences.zh: 又料擇伏瘴舊獠與州兵之任戰者，廢遣獰耄什三四，士無敢怨。

translations.literal: He also selected from the old Liao in malarial regions and from the prefectural troops those fit for battle, dismissing three or four tenths of the fierce and aged; the soldiers dared not complain.
translations.idiomatic: He picked out the able fighters among the old tribal levies in the fever country and the prefectural garrisons, cashiering three or four men in ten who were too old or too unruly—and not a soldier dared protest.

sentences.zh: 又請甲人于安定，弓人河中，弩人浙西。

translations.literal: He also requisitioned armor-makers from Dingzhou, bow-makers from Hezhong, and crossbow-makers from Zhexi.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent for armorers from Dingzhou, bowyers from Hezhong, and crossbow-makers from Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 繇是蜀之器械皆犀銳。

translations.literal: From this Shu's weapons and equipment were all exceptionally sharp.
translations.idiomatic: From that point on, every weapon in Shu was forged to a razor edge.

sentences.zh: 率戶二百取一人，使習戰，貸勿事，緩則農，急則戰，謂之「雄邊子弟」。

translations.literal: For every two hundred households he took one man to train for battle, exempting him from corvée; in peacetime they farmed, in emergency they fought—they were called "Frontier Sons."
translations.idiomatic: From every two hundred households he drafted one man for military training, exempt from corvée labor—farming in quiet times, fighting in crisis. They were called the "Frontier Sons."

sentences.zh: 其精兵曰南燕保義、保惠、兩河慕義、左右連弩；

translations.literal: The elite troops were named Southern Yan, Baoyi, Baohui, Two Rivers Muyi, and Left and Right Crossbow.
translations.idiomatic: His crack infantry bore names like Southern Yan, Loyal Guard, Loyal Benevolence, Two Rivers Aspiring Loyalty, and the Left and Right Crossbow corps.

sentences.zh: 騎士曰飛星、鷙擊、奇鋒、流電、霆聲、突騎。

translations.literal: The cavalry were named Flying Star, Fierce Strike, Strange Edge, Flowing Lightning, Thunder Sound, and Charge Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His cavalry units were called Flying Star, Fierce Assault, Strange Edge, Flowing Lightning, Thunderclap, and Shock Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 總十一軍。

translations.literal: In all there were eleven armies.
translations.idiomatic: Eleven armies in all.

sentences.zh: 築杖義城，以制大度、青溪關之阻；

translations.literal: He built Zhangyi Fort to control the barrier of the Dudu and Qingxi passes.
translations.idiomatic: He fortified Zhangyi to hold the strategic choke points at Dudu and Qingxi.

sentences.zh: 作禦侮城，以控榮經犄角勢；

translations.literal: He built Yuwu Fort to control the pincer position of Rong and Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He raised Yuwu Fort to dominate the mutual-support positions at Rong and Jing.

sentences.zh: 作柔遠城，以厄西山吐蕃；

translations.literal: He built Rouyuan Fort to block Tibet in the western mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He built Rouyuan Fort to pin down the Tibetans in the western hills.

sentences.zh: 復邛崍關，徙巂州治台登，以奪蠻險。

translations.literal: He restored Qionglai Pass, moved Xi prefecture's seat to Taideng, to seize the barbarians' strategic terrain.
translations.idiomatic: He reopened Qionglai Pass and moved the seat of Xi prefecture to Taideng, retaking terrain the barbarians had held.

sentences.zh: 舊制，歲抄運內粟贍黎、巂州，起嘉、眉，道陽山江，而達大度，乃分餉諸戍。

translations.literal: Under the old system, each year in the autumn grain from the interior was transported to supply Li and Xi prefectures, starting from Jia and Mei, passing Yangshan River, reaching Dudu, and then distributed to the garrison posts.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, grain from the interior was shipped each autumn to feed Li and Xi prefectures—loaded at Jia and Mei, carried along the Yangshan River to Dudu, then parcelled out to the frontier garrisons.

sentences.zh: 常以盛夏至，地苦瘴毒，輦夫多死。

translations.literal: It usually arrived in midsummer; the region was plagued by malarial poison, and many transport bearers died.
translations.idiomatic: The convoys usually arrived in the height of summer, when malarial fevers ravaged the route and porters died by the score.

sentences.zh: 德裕命轉邛、雅粟，以十月為漕始，先夏而至，以佐陽山之運，饋者不涉炎月，遠民乃安。

translations.literal: Deyu ordered grain to be transported from Qiong and Ya, with the tenth month as the start of transport, arriving before summer to supplement the Yangshan route; bearers no longer passed through the hot months, and the distant people were at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu rerouted grain from Qiong and Ya, starting transport in the tenth month so supplies reached the frontier before summer and eased the Yangshan haul. Porters no longer marched through the fever months, and the border population finally had breathing room.

sentences.zh: 蜀人多鬻女為人妾，德裕為著科約：凡十三而上，執三年勞；

translations.literal: Many in Shu sold their daughters as concubines; Deyu established regulations: for those thirteen and above, three years of service.
translations.idiomatic: Many families in Shu sold daughters into concubinage; Deyu drew up rules fixing the term of service at three years for girls thirteen and older.

sentences.zh: 下者，五歲；

translations.literal: For those below, five years.
translations.idiomatic: For younger girls, five years.

sentences.zh: 及期則歸之父母。

translations.literal: When the term expired they were returned to their parents.
translations.idiomatic: When the term expired, they were sent back to their parents.

sentences.zh: 毀屬下浮屠私廬數千，以地予農。

translations.literal: He destroyed thousands of private Buddhist monasteries under his jurisdiction and gave the land to farmers.
translations.idiomatic: He demolished thousands of unauthorized Buddhist shrines in his jurisdiction and turned the land over to farmers.

sentences.zh: 蜀先主祠旁有猱村，其民剔髮若浮屠者，畜妻子自如，德裕下令禁止。

translations.literal: Beside the shrine of the Shu Founding Lord was Monkey Village, whose people shaved their heads like Buddhists yet kept wives and children as they pleased; Deyu ordered this forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Near the shrine of Liu Bei stood Monkey Village, where men shaved their heads like monks while keeping wives and children as they saw fit; Deyu banned the practice outright.

sentences.zh: 蜀風大變。

translations.literal: The customs of Shu changed greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Customs throughout Shu changed overnight.

sentences.zh: 於是二邊浸懼，南詔請還所俘掠四千人，吐蕃維州將悉怛謀以城降。

translations.literal: Thereupon both frontiers grew increasingly fearful; Nanzhao requested to return four thousand captives they had seized, and the Tibetan general Sidu Mou of Weizhou surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Both frontiers now feared him. Nanzhao offered to return four thousand captives, and Sidu Mou, the Tibetan commander at Weizhou, surrendered his fortress.

sentences.zh: 維距成都四百里，因山為固，東北繇索叢嶺而下二百里，地無險，走長川不三千里，直吐蕃之牙，異時戍之，以制虜入者也。

translations.literal: Wei was four hundred li from Chengdu, fortified by mountains; northeast down from Suocong Ridge for two hundred li the terrain offered no barriers—a long valley of less than three thousand li led straight to Tibet's royal seat; in earlier times it was garrisoned to block enemy incursions.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhou lay four hundred li from Chengdu, its defenses anchored in the mountains. Two hundred li northeast, beyond Suocong Ridge, the land flattened into an open valley; within three thousand li it ran straight to the Tibetan capital. In earlier times the court had garrisoned it precisely to block invaders at that gate.

sentences.zh: 德裕既得之，即發兵以守，且陳出師之利。

translations.literal: Once Deyu had it, he immediately sent troops to garrison it and set forth the advantages of launching a campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The moment he held Weizhou, Deyu sent troops to occupy it and memorialized the court on the strategic gains of a full campaign.

sentences.zh: 僧孺居中沮其功，命返悉怛謀於虜，以信所盟，德裕終身以為恨。

translations.literal: Sengru in the capital blocked this achievement, ordering Sidu Mou returned to the enemy to honor their alliance; Deyu regretted this for life.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Sengru at court blocked the plan, ordering Sidu Mou handed back to the Tibetans to honor a prior treaty. Deyu never forgave it.

sentences.zh: 會監軍使王踐言入朝，盛言悉怛謀死，拒遠人向化意。

translations.literal: When the military supervisor Wang Jianyan came to court, he spoke at length of Sidu Mou's death, saying it rejected the will of distant peoples to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When the army supervisor Wang Jianyan reached the capital, he spoke passionately of Sidu Mou's execution—how it had spurned every distant people who wished to come over to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 帝亦悔之，即以兵部尚書召，俄拜中書門下平章事，封贊皇縣伯。

translations.literal: The emperor also regretted it and summoned him as Minister of War; soon he was appointed Grand Counselor of the Secretariat and Chancellery and enfeoffed as Baron of Zanhuang County.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor shared his regret and recalled Deyu as Minister of War; soon afterward he was made Grand Counselor and enfeoffed as Baron of Zanhuang.

sentences.zh: 故事，丞郎詣宰相，須少間乃敢通，郎官非公事不敢謁。

translations.literal: By precedent, when vice directors and bureau directors called on the chief minister, they had to wait a while before daring to announce themselves; bureau officials did not dare visit without official business.
translations.idiomatic: By long-standing custom, vice directors and bureau directors who called on the chief minister waited in an antechamber before being announced; junior officials did not dare visit without official business.

sentences.zh: 李宗閔時，往往通賓客。

translations.literal: During Li Zongmin's tenure, visitors and guests were often admitted directly.
translations.idiomatic: Under Li Zongmin, guests and callers were waved straight through.

sentences.zh: 李聽為太子太傅，招所善載酒集宗閔閣，酣醉乃去。

translations.literal: Li Ting as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent would invite his favorites with wine to gather at Zongmin's pavilion, leaving only when thoroughly drunk.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ting, Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent, would bring wine and his cronies to Zongmin's office and stay until everyone was drunk.

sentences.zh: 至德裕，則喻御史：「有以事見宰相，必先白台乃聽。

translations.literal: When Deyu came to office, he instructed the censor: "Anyone wishing to see the chief minister on business must first report to the Censorate before being admitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Deyu took over, he told the censors: "Anyone who wishes to see the chief minister on business must first notify the Censorate and receive permission.

sentences.zh: 凡罷朝，由龍尾道趨出。

translations.literal: After court all must hurry out via the Dragon Tail Road."
translations.idiomatic: After court adjourns, everyone must leave promptly by the Dragon Tail Road."

sentences.zh: 」遂無輒至閣者。

translations.literal: Thus none came casually to the pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: After that, no one dropped in uninvited.

sentences.zh: 又罷京兆築沙堤、兩街上朝衛兵。

translations.literal: He also abolished the Jingzhao sand embankment construction and the street guard troops for court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: He also ended the Jingzhao sand-dike works and the street guards posted for morning court.

sentences.zh: 常建言：「朝廷惟邪正二途，正必去邪，邪必害正。

translations.literal: He often advised: "The court has only two paths, the upright and the corrupt; the upright must drive out the corrupt, and the corrupt must harm the upright.
translations.idiomatic: He often warned the emperor: "The court admits only two kinds of men—the upright and the corrupt. The upright must expel the corrupt, and the corrupt will always seek to destroy the upright.

sentences.zh: 然其辭皆若可聽，願審所取捨。

translations.literal: Yet their words all sound persuasive—I beg you to examine carefully what you accept and reject.
translations.idiomatic: Yet both sides speak persuasively. I beg Your Majesty to weigh each voice with care.

sentences.zh: 不然，二者並進，雖聖賢經營，無繇成功。

translations.literal: Otherwise, if both advance together, even a sage could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: If both are allowed to advance together, not even a sage could govern successfully.

sentences.zh: 」俄而宗閔罷，德裕代為中書侍郎、集賢殿大學士。

translations.literal: Soon Li Zongmin was dismissed, and Deyu replaced him as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li Zongmin was removed, and Deyu succeeded him as Vice Director of the Secretariat and Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 始，二省符江淮大賈，使主堂廚食利，因是挾貲行天下，所至州鎮為右客，富人倚以自高。

translations.literal: Initially the Two Departments issued credentials to great merchants from the Jiang-Huai region to manage the chancellor's kitchen profits; thus armed with capital they traveled the empire, becoming honored guests wherever they went, and the wealthy relied on them for prestige.
translations.idiomatic: For years the Two Departments had licensed great Jiang-Huai merchants to run the chancellery kitchens for profit. Armed with those credentials and capital, they traveled the empire as honored guests of every prefecture and garrison, and the rich used them to burnish their status.

sentences.zh: 德裕一切罷之。

translations.literal: Deyu abolished all of this.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu abolished the practice entirely.

sentences.zh: 後帝暴感風，害語言。

translations.literal: Later the emperor suddenly contracted wind illness that impaired his speech.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor was suddenly stricken with a wind disorder that left him unable to speak clearly.

sentences.zh: 鄭注始因王守澄以藥進，帝少間，又薦李訓使待詔，帝欲授諫官，德裕曰：「昔諸葛亮有言：'親賢臣，遠小人，先漢所以興隆也。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhu first gained entry through Wang Shoucheng with medicines; after the emperor recovered slightly, he also recommended Li Xun as a draft attendant; when the emperor wished to appoint him a remonstrance official, Deyu said: "Zhuge Liang once said: 'Honor worthy ministers and keep petty men at a distance—this is why the Former Han flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhu had first entered court through Wang Shoucheng, offering medicines; when the emperor recovered somewhat, Zhu also recommended Li Xun as a draft attendant. When the emperor proposed making Xun a remonstrance official, Deyu objected: "Zhuge Liang once said, 'Honor worthy ministers and keep petty men at a distance—that is why the Former Han rose.

sentences.zh: 親小人，遠賢士，後漢所以傾頹也。

translations.literal: Honor petty men and keep worthy scholars at a distance—this is why the Later Han fell into ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Honor petty men and keep worthy scholars at a distance—that is why the Later Han collapsed.

sentences.zh: '今訓小人，頃咎惡暴天下，不宜引致左右。

translations.literal: Li Xun is a petty man whose recent crimes are notorious throughout the empire—he should not be brought close to Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun is a petty man whose recent crimes are known throughout the empire. He must not be brought close to Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「人誰無過，當容其改。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Who among men has no faults? We should allow him to reform.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Who among men has no faults? We should allow him to reform.

sentences.zh: 且逢吉嘗言之。

translations.literal: Besides, Fengji once spoke in his favor.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, Li Fengji has already spoken in his favor.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「聖賢則有改過，若訓天資奸邪，尚何能改？

translations.literal: Deyu replied: "Sages can reform their faults—but with Xun's innate treachery, how could he change?
translations.idiomatic: Deyu replied, "Sages can reform their faults—but Xun is treacherous by nature. How could he change?

sentences.zh: 逢吉位宰相，而顧愛凶回，以累陛下，亦罪人也。

translations.literal: Fengji holds the post of chief minister yet cherishes vicious traitors, bringing harm to Your Majesty—he too is guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Fengji sits as chief minister yet coddles vicious men, bringing harm upon Your Majesty. He too is guilty.

sentences.zh: 」帝語王涯別與官，德裕搖手止涯，帝適見，不懌，訓、注皆怨，即復召宗閔輔政，拜德裕為興元節度使。

translations.literal: The emperor told Wang Ya to give Xun a different office; Deyu waved his hand to stop Wang Ya—the emperor happened to see this and was displeased; Xun and Zhu both resented it, and Li Zongmin was recalled to assist in governance while Deyu was appointed military governor of Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Wang Ya to give Xun another post. Deyu waved him off—and the emperor saw it and took offense. Xun and Zhu both nursed a grudge. Li Zongmin was recalled to govern, and Deyu was posted out as military governor of Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 入見帝，自陳願留闕下，復拜兵部尚書。

translations.literal: On entering to see the emperor, he stated his wish to remain at court and was again appointed Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: When he came before the emperor, Deyu asked to remain at court and was again appointed Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 宗閔奏：「命已行，不可止。

translations.literal: Li Zongmin memorialized: "The order has already been issued and cannot be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongmin memorialized: "The order has already gone out and cannot be revoked.

sentences.zh: 」更徙鎮海軍以代王璠。

translations.literal: Instead he was transferred to Zhenhai Army to replace Wang Fan.
translations.idiomatic: Instead Deyu was transferred to Zhenhai to replace Wang Fan.

sentences.zh: 先是太和中，漳王養母杜仲陽歸浙西，有詔在所存問。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Taihe era, the Prince of Zhang's foster mother Du Zhongyang returned to Zhexi; an edict ordered local officials to inquire after her welfare.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Taihe era, the Prince of Zhang's foster mother Du Zhongyang had returned to Zhexi, and an edict ordered the local authorities to look after her.

sentences.zh: 時德裕被召，乃檄留後使如詔書。

translations.literal: At that time Deyu had been summoned to court and left orders with his acting governor to carry out the edict.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu had already been summoned to the capital and left written orders with his acting governor to carry out the edict.

sentences.zh: 璠入為尚書左丞，而漳王以罪廢死，因與戶部侍郎李漢共譖德裕嘗賂仲陽導王為不軌。

translations.literal: Fan entered the capital as Vice Director of the Left Department of the Ministry of Revenue; when the Prince of Zhang was deposed and executed for crimes, Fan together with Vice Minister of Revenue Li Han slandered Deyu, claiming he had bribed Zhongyang to guide the prince in treason.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Fan entered the capital as Vice Director of the Left Department. When the Prince of Zhang was deposed and executed, Fan joined Vice Minister of Revenue Li Han in accusing Deyu of bribing Zhongyang to lead the prince into treason.

sentences.zh: 帝惑其言，召王涯、李固言、路隋質之，注、璠、漢三人者語益堅，獨隋言：「德裕大臣，不宜有此。

translations.literal: The emperor was swayed and summoned Wang Ya, Li Guyuan, and Lu Sui to question them; Zhu, Fan, and Han spoke more insistently, but only Lu Sui said: "Deyu is a great minister—it is unfitting that he would do such a thing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was swayed and summoned Wang Ya, Li Guyuan, and Lu Sui to verify the charges. Zheng Zhu, Fan, and Han pressed their case harder, but Lu Sui alone said, "Deyu is a senior minister. Such conduct is unthinkable.

sentences.zh: 」讒焰少衰。

translations.literal: The flames of slander subsided somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: The force of the slander eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 遂貶德裕為太子賓客，分司東都。

translations.literal: Deyu was demoted to Guest of the Heir Apparent with duty at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu was demoted to Guest of the Heir Apparent with duty at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 復貶袁州長史，隋亦免宰相。

translations.literal: He was further demoted to Administrator of Yuan Prefecture; Lu Sui was also removed from the chancellorship.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted again to administrator of Yuan prefecture, and Lu Sui was also stripped of the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 未幾，宗閔以罪斥，而注、訓等亂敗。

translations.literal: Before long Li Zongmin was expelled for crimes, and Zhu, Xun, and their faction met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Zongmin was expelled for crimes, and Zheng Zhu, Li Xun, and their faction were destroyed in the upheaval.

sentences.zh: 帝追悟德裕以誣構逐，乃徙滁州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor came to realize Deyu had been driven out on fabricated charges and transferred him to Prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor came to see that Deyu had been driven out on false charges and transferred him to prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 又以太子賓客分司東都。

translations.literal: He was again made Guest of the Heir Apparent with duty at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Guest of the Heir Apparent with duty at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 開成初，帝從容語宰相：「朝廷豈有遺事乎？

translations.literal: At the start of the Kaicheng era, the emperor casually asked the chief ministers: "Are there any overlooked matters at court?
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaicheng era, the emperor asked his chief ministers casually, "Is there anything the court has left undone?

sentences.zh: 」眾皆以宋申錫對。

translations.literal: All answered with Song Shenxi.
translations.idiomatic: They all named Song Shenxi.

sentences.zh: 帝俯首涕數行下，曰：「當此時，兄弟不相保，況申錫邪？

translations.literal: The emperor bowed his head, tears streaming down, and said: "At that time, even brothers could not protect one another—how much less Shenxi?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bowed his head, tears running down his face, and said, "In those days even brothers could not protect one another—how much less could Shenxi?

sentences.zh: 有司為我褒顯之。

translations.literal: Have the authorities honor and display his merit for me.
translations.idiomatic: Let the authorities honor and commemorate him for me.

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「德裕亦申錫比也。

translations.literal: He also said: "Deyu is in the same case as Shenxi.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Deyu suffered the same injustice as Shenxi.

sentences.zh: 」起為浙西觀察使。

translations.literal: Deyu was recalled as Governor of Zhexi.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu was recalled as governor of Zhexi.

sentences.zh: 後對學士禁中，黎埴頓首言：「德裕與宗閔皆逐，而獨三進官。

translations.literal: Later, when meeting academicians in the palace, Li Zhi prostrated himself and said: "Deyu and Zongmin were both expelled, yet Deyu alone has been promoted three times.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when meeting academicians in the palace, Li Zhi prostrated himself and said, "Deyu and Zongmin were both driven out, yet Deyu alone has been promoted three times.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「彼嘗進鄭注，而德裕欲殺之，今當以官與何人？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "They once promoted Zheng Zhu, while Deyu wanted to kill him—to whom should I give office now?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "They once promoted Zheng Zhu, while Deyu wanted him dead. To whom should I give office now?

sentences.zh: 」埴懼而出。

translations.literal: Li Zhi fled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi withdrew in fear.

sentences.zh: 又指坐扆前示宰相曰：「此德裕爭鄭注處。

translations.literal: The emperor also pointed to the seat before the screen and showed the chief ministers: "This is where Deyu argued against Zheng Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also pointed to the seat before the screen and told the chief ministers, "This is where Deyu argued against Zheng Zhu.

translations.literal: Such he said.
translations.idiomatic: So he spoke, and said no more.

sentences.zh: 德裕三在浙西，出入十年，遷淮南節度使，代牛僧孺。

translations.literal: Deyu served three times in Zhexi, coming and going over ten years, then was transferred as military governor of Huainan to replace Niu Sengru.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu served three terms in Zhexi over the course of ten years, then was transferred to Huainan as military governor to replace Niu Sengru.

sentences.zh: 僧孺聞之，以軍事付其副張鷺，即馳去。

translations.literal: When Sengru heard this, he handed military affairs to his deputy Zhang Lu and immediately galloped away.
translations.idiomatic: When Sengru heard the news, he handed military affairs to his deputy Zhang Lu and rode off at once.

sentences.zh: 淮南府錢八十萬緡，德裕奏言止四十萬，為鷺用其半。

translations.literal: The Huainan headquarters held eight hundred thousand strings of cash; Deyu memorialized that there were only four hundred thousand, half of which Zhang Lu had spent.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainan headquarters treasury held eight hundred thousand strings of cash; Deyu reported that only four hundred thousand remained, half of which Zhang Lu had already spent.

sentences.zh: 僧孺訴於帝，而諫官姚合、魏謨等共劾奏德裕挾私怨沮傷僧孺，帝置章不下，詔德裕覆實。

translations.literal: Sengru appealed to the emperor; remonstrance officials Yao He, Wei Mo, and others jointly impeached Deyu for harboring private grudges and slandering Sengru; the emperor withheld the memorial and ordered Deyu to verify the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Sengru appealed to the emperor. Remonstrance officials Yao He, Wei Mo, and others jointly impeached Deyu for letting private resentment drive a smear against Sengru. The emperor withheld the memorial and ordered Deyu to verify the facts.

sentences.zh: 德裕上言：「諸鎮更代，例殺半數以備水旱、助軍費。

translations.literal: Deyu submitted: "When military governors succeed one another, it is customary to retain half the funds for flood, drought, and military expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu submitted: "When military governors succeed one another, it is customary to retain half the treasury for flood relief, drought relief, and military expenses.

sentences.zh: 因索王播、段文昌、崔從相授簿最具在。

translations.literal: He then requested the handover ledgers of Wang Bo, Duan Wenchang, and Cui Cong—all were intact.
translations.idiomatic: He then requested the handover ledgers of Wang Bo, Duan Wenchang, and Cui Cong—all were intact and on file.

sentences.zh: 惟從死官下，僧孺代之，其所殺數最多。

translations.literal: Only Cui Cong died in office and Sengru replaced him—he retained the largest amount.
translations.idiomatic: Only Cui Cong had died in office and been succeeded by Sengru, who had retained the largest share.

sentences.zh: 」即自劾「始至鎮，失於用例，不敢妄」，遂待罪，有詔釋之。

translations.literal: Deyu then impeached himself: "Having just arrived, I failed to follow precedent and did not dare act recklessly"; he awaited punishment, and an edict released him.
translations.idiomatic: He then impeached himself: "Having just arrived, I failed to follow established practice and did not dare act rashly." He awaited judgment, and an edict cleared him.

sentences.zh: 武宗立，召為門下侍郎、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wuzong ascended, Deyu was summoned as Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wuzong ascended the throne, Deyu was summoned as Vice Director of the Chancellery and Grand Counselor.

sentences.zh: 既入謝，即進戒帝：「辨邪正，專委任，而後朝廷治。

translations.literal: After entering to give thanks, he immediately admonished the emperor: "Distinguish the corrupt from the upright, delegate authority fully—only then will the court be well governed.
translations.idiomatic: After entering to give thanks, he immediately admonished the emperor: "Distinguish the corrupt from the upright and delegate authority resolutely—only then can the court be well governed.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗為先帝言之，不見用。

translations.literal: I once spoke thus to the late emperor, but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: I once spoke the same words to the late emperor, but was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 夫正人既呼小人為邪，小人亦謂正人為邪，何以辨之？

translations.literal: The upright call petty men corrupt, and petty men call the upright corrupt—how are they to be distinguished?
translations.idiomatic: The upright call petty men corrupt, and petty men call the upright corrupt—how is one to tell them apart?

sentences.zh: 請借物為諭，松柏之為木，孤生勁特，無所因倚。

translations.literal: Permit me to illustrate with a comparison: pine and cypress as trees grow alone, strong and upright, relying on nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Permit me to illustrate with a comparison: pine and cypress grow alone—strong, upright, relying on nothing.

sentences.zh: 蘿蔦則不然，弱不能立，必附它木。

translations.literal: Creepers are not so—they are too weak to stand alone and must cling to another tree.
translations.idiomatic: Creepers are not like that—they are too weak to stand on their own and must cling to another tree.

sentences.zh: 故正人一心事君，無待於助。

translations.literal: Therefore upright men serve the ruler with undivided hearts and need no assistance.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore upright men serve the ruler with undivided loyalty and need no outside support.

sentences.zh: 邪人必更為黨，以相蔽欺。

translations.literal: Corrupt men will inevitably form factions to shield and deceive one another.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt men inevitably band together in factions, shielding and deceiving one another.

sentences.zh: 君人者以是辨之，則無惑矣。

translations.literal: Let the ruler distinguish them by this, and he will be free of confusion.
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler distinguishes them by this test, he will no longer be deceived.

sentences.zh: 」又謂治亂系信任，引齊桓公問管仲所以害霸者，仲對琴瑟笙竽、弋獵馳騁，非害霸者；

translations.literal: " He also said that order and disorder depend on trust, citing Duke Huan of Qi's question to Guan Zhong about what harms hegemony—Guan replied that lutes, zithers, sheng and yu pipes, archery, hunting, and racing are not what harms hegemony;
translations.idiomatic: " He also said that order and disorder depend on trust, citing Duke Huan of Qi's question to Guan Zhong about what truly harms hegemony. Guan Zhong replied that music, hunting, and racing are not what harms hegemony;

sentences.zh: 惟知人不能舉，舉不能任，任而又雜以小人，害霸也。

translations.literal: Only when one knows men but cannot promote them, promotes but cannot employ them, or employs them yet mixes in petty men—this harms hegemony.
translations.idiomatic: Only failing to know and promote the right men, failing to entrust them with real authority, or mixing petty men among them—this is what harms hegemony.

sentences.zh: 「太、玄、德、憲四宗皆盛朝，其始臨禦，自視若堯、舜，浸久則不及初，陛下知其然乎？

translations.literal: "The four reigns of Taizong, Xuanzong, Dezong, and Xianzong were all flourishing courts; at first when they assumed rule they saw themselves as Yao and Shun, yet over time they fell short of the beginning—Your Majesty, do you know why?
translations.idiomatic: "The reigns of Taizong, Xuanzong, Dezong, and Xianzong were all times of greatness. At first each emperor took the throne seeing himself as another Yao or Shun, yet in time each fell short of his early promise—Your Majesty, do you know why?

sentences.zh: 始一委輔相，故賢者得盡心。

translations.literal: At first they fully delegated to chief ministers, so the worthy could give their full devotion.
translations.idiomatic: At first they fully entrusted affairs to their chief ministers, so worthy men could serve with their whole hearts.

sentences.zh: 久則小人並進，造黨與，亂視聽，故上疑而不專。

translations.literal: Over time petty men advanced together, formed factions, and confused what the ruler saw and heard, so the ruler grew suspicious and no longer entrusted authority fully.
translations.idiomatic: In time petty men gained ground together, formed factions, and clouded the emperor's judgment, until the throne grew suspicious and hesitated to delegate.

sentences.zh: 政去宰相則不治矣。

translations.literal: When governance departs from the chief minister, there can be no good order.
translations.idiomatic: When governance no longer rests with the chief minister, the state cannot be well governed.

sentences.zh: 在德宗最甚，晚節宰相惟奉行詔書，所與圖事者，李齊運、裴延齡、韋渠牟等，訖今謂之亂政。

translations.literal: This was worst under Dezong; in his later years the chief minister merely carried out edicts, while those with whom he consulted on affairs were Li Qiyun, Pei Yanling, Wei Qiumou, and the like—down to this day they are called a disordered government.
translations.idiomatic: This was worst under Emperor Dezong. In his later years the chief minister merely executed edicts, while those he actually consulted were Li Qiyun, Pei Yanling, Wei Qiumou, and the like—down to this day that is remembered as a disordered government.

sentences.zh: 夫輔相有欺罔不忠，當亟免，忠而材者屬任之。

translations.literal: When a chief minister is deceitful and disloyal, he should be removed at once; loyal and capable men should be entrusted in succession.
translations.idiomatic: When a chief minister is deceitful and disloyal, remove him at once and entrust loyal and capable men in his place.

sentences.zh: 政無它門，天下安有不治？

translations.literal: If governance has no other outlet, how could the realm fail to be well governed?
translations.idiomatic: If governance has no other channel, how could the realm fail to be well governed?

sentences.zh: 先帝任人，始皆回容，積纖微以至誅貶。

translations.literal: The late emperor in employing men at first always showed tolerance, but accumulated minute faults until execution and demotion.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor, when employing men, at first always showed forbearance, then piled up minor faults until men were executed or demoted.

sentences.zh: 誠使雖小過必知而改之，君臣無猜，則讒邪不幹其間矣。

translations.literal: If truly even small faults were known and corrected, and ruler and minister were free of suspicion, then slander and corruption could not interfere between them.
translations.idiomatic: If even small faults were acknowledged and corrected, and ruler and minister were free of mutual suspicion, slander and corruption could not come between them.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「開元初，輔相率三考輒去，雖姚崇、宋璟不能逾。

translations.literal: " He also said: "In the early Kaiyuan era, chief ministers as a rule left after three performance reviews; even Yao Chong and Song Jing could not exceed this.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said: "In the early Kaiyuan era, chief ministers routinely left office after three performance reviews—even Yao Chong and Song Jing could not stay longer.

sentences.zh: 至李林甫，秉權乃十九年，遂及禍敗。

translations.literal: When Li Linfu came, he held power for nineteen years, and thus disaster followed.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Linfu came to power he held it for nineteen years, and disaster followed.

sentences.zh: 是知亟進罷宰相，使政在中書，誠治本也。

translations.literal: From this one knows that promptly advancing and dismissing chief ministers, keeping governance in the Secretariat, is truly the root of good order.
translations.idiomatic: This shows that promptly appointing and dismissing chief ministers and keeping governance in the Secretariat is truly the foundation of good order.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗疑楊嗣復、李玨顧望不忠，遣使殺之。

translations.literal: The emperor once suspected Yang Sifu and Li Jue of hesitation and disloyalty and dispatched envoys to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once suspected Yang Sifu and Li Jue of hedging and disloyalty and sent envoys to have them killed.

sentences.zh: 德裕知帝性剛而果於斷，即率三宰相見延英，嗚咽流涕曰：「昔太宗、德宗誅大臣，未嘗不悔。

translations.literal: Deyu knew the emperor's nature was firm and decisive; he immediately led the three chief ministers to see him at Yanying Hall, weeping as he said: "In the past when Taizong and Dezong executed great ministers, they never failed to regret it.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu knew the emperor was resolute and swift to decide. He immediately led the three chief ministers into Yanying Hall, weeping as he said: "When Taizong and Dezong put great ministers to death, they always came to regret it.

sentences.zh: 臣欲陛下全活之，無異時恨。

translations.literal: Your subject wishes Your Majesty to preserve their lives entirely, lest there be regret later.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to spare their lives so you will not regret it later.

sentences.zh: 使二人罪惡暴著，天下共疾之。

translations.literal: Let the crimes of the two men be fully exposed, and all under Heaven together despise them.
translations.idiomatic: Let their crimes be fully exposed so that all under Heaven despises them together.

sentences.zh: 」帝不許，德裕伏不起。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not agree; Deyu prostrated himself and would not rise.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor refused. Deyu prostrated himself and would not rise.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「為公等赦之。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "For your sake I pardon them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "For your sake I pardon them.

sentences.zh: 」德裕降拜升坐。

translations.literal: " Deyu descended, bowed, and resumed his seat.
translations.idiomatic: " Deyu descended, bowed, and resumed his seat.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「如令諫官論爭，雖千疏，我不赦。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If remonstrance officials had argued, even with a thousand memorials, I would not have pardoned them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "If the remonstrance officials had argued the point, even with a thousand memorials, I would not have pardoned them.

sentences.zh: 」德裕重拜。

translations.literal: " Deyu bowed again deeply.
translations.idiomatic: " Deyu bowed again deeply.

sentences.zh: 因追還使者，嗣復等乃免。

translations.literal: He then recalled the envoys, and Sifu and the others were spared.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then recalled the envoys, and Sifu and the others were spared.

sentences.zh: 時帝數出畋遊，暮夜乃還，德裕上言；

translations.literal: At that time the emperor often went out hunting and did not return until night; Deyu submitted a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the emperor often went out hunting and did not return until night. Deyu submitted a memorial:

sentences.zh: 「人君動法於日，故出而視朝，入而燕息。

translations.literal: "The ruler's movements follow the pattern of the day; therefore he goes out to hold court and returns to rest at ease.
translations.idiomatic: "The ruler's conduct should follow the rhythm of the day—going out to hold court and returning to rest at leisure.

sentences.zh: 《傳》曰：'君就房有常節。

translations.literal: The Classic of History says: 'The ruler's retiring to the inner chambers has fixed rules.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents of Antiquity says: 'The ruler's retiring to the inner chambers has fixed rules.

sentences.zh: '惟深察古誼，毋繼以夜。

translations.literal: ' Only by deeply examining ancient principles, and not extending activities into the night.
translations.idiomatic: ' Only by deeply heeding ancient principle and not extending your activities into the night.

sentences.zh: 側聞五星失度，恐天以是勤勤儆戒。

translations.literal: I have heard on the side that the five planets are out of their courses—I fear Heaven uses this to warn you repeatedly and diligently.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the five planets are out of their proper courses. I fear Heaven is warning you through this diligent sign.

sentences.zh: 《詩》曰：'敬天之渝，不敢馳驅。

translations.literal: The Odes say: 'In reverence for Heaven's reproof, I dare not race about.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes say: 'In reverence for Heaven's reproof, I dare not race about.

sentences.zh: '願節田游，承天意。

translations.literal: ' I pray you restrain your hunting and comply with Heaven's will.
translations.idiomatic: ' I pray you restrain your hunting and comply with Heaven's will.

sentences.zh: 」尋冊拜司空。

translations.literal: " Soon afterward he was enfeoffed and appointed Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward he was enfeoffed and appointed Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 回鶻自開成時為黠戛斯所破。

translations.literal: The Uighurs had been shattered by the Kirghiz since the Kaicheng era.
translations.idiomatic: The Uighurs had been shattered by the Kirghiz since the Kaicheng era.

sentences.zh: 會昌後，烏介可汗挾公主牙塞下，種族大饑，以弱口、重器易粟于邊。

translations.literal: After Huichang, Khan Wujie held the princess at Yashai; his people suffered great famine and exchanged dependents and heavy goods for grain at the border.
translations.idiomatic: After Huichang, Khan Wujie held the princess at Yashai. His people suffered grievous famine and traded dependents and valuables for grain at the border.

sentences.zh: 退渾、党項利虜掠，因天德軍使田牟上言，願以部落兵擊之。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun and Tangut profited from looting the invaders; through Tian Mu, military commissioner of Tiande Army, they submitted that they wished to attack with tribal troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun and Tangut saw profit in raiding the refugees. Tian Mu, commander of the Tiande Army, submitted that they wished to attack with tribal troops.

sentences.zh: 議者請可其言。

translations.literal: Those in deliberation asked that this proposal be approved.
translations.idiomatic: Those deliberating urged that the proposal be approved.

sentences.zh: 德裕曰：「回鶻于國嘗有功，以窮來歸，未輒擾邊，遽伐之，非漢宣帝待呼韓之義。

translations.literal: Deyu said: "The Uighurs once served the state with merit; coming in destitution to submit, they have not yet disturbed the border—to attack them hastily is not in the spirit of how Emperor Xuan of Han treated Huhanye.
