translations.idiomatic: Deyu said: "The Uighurs once served our state with merit. They have come to us in destitution and have not yet disturbed the border—to attack them hastily would betray the spirit in which Emperor Xuan of Han treated Huhanye.

sentences.zh: 不如與之食，以待其變。

translations.literal: Better to give them food and wait for changes.
translations.idiomatic: Better to give them food and wait to see how matters develop.

sentences.zh: 」陳夷行曰：「資盜糧，非計也，不如擊之便。

translations.literal: " Chen Yixing said: "Feeding robbers is no plan—better to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: " Chen Yixing said: "To supply bandits with grain is no strategy—it would be better to attack them.

sentences.zh: 」德裕曰：「沙陀、退渾，不可恃也。

translations.literal: " Deyu said: "The Shatuo and Tuyuhun cannot be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: " Deyu said: "The Shatuo and Tuyuhun cannot be relied upon.

sentences.zh: 夫見利則進，遇敵則走，雜虜之常態，孰肯為國家用邪？

translations.literal: When they see profit they advance; when they meet the enemy they flee—this is the usual conduct of mixed barbarians; who would truly serve the state?
translations.idiomatic: When they see profit they advance; when they meet the enemy they flee—that is the usual way of such frontier tribes. Who would truly fight for the state?

sentences.zh: 天德兵素弱，以一城與勁虜確，無不敗。

translations.literal: The Tiande troops have always been weak; to pit one fortress against fierce barbarians in a standoff—there can be no victory.
translations.idiomatic: The Tiande garrison has always been weak. To pit one fortress against fierce steppe warriors in open battle is to invite defeat.

sentences.zh: 請詔牟無聽諸戎計。

translations.literal: I ask that an edict command Mu not to heed the barbarians' plan.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that an edict command Mu not to heed the barbarians' plan.

sentences.zh: 」帝於是貸粟二萬斛。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon loaned twenty thousand bushels of grain.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor thereupon loaned them twenty thousand bushels of grain.

sentences.zh: 會嗢沒斯殺赤心以降，赤心兵潰去。

translations.literal: When Wamosi killed Chixin and surrendered, Chixin's soldiers broke and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Wamosi killed Chixin and surrendered, Chixin's forces broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 於是回鶻勢窮，數丐羊馬，欲藉兵復故地，又願假天德城以舍公主，帝不許。

translations.literal: The Uighurs were then at their limit; they repeatedly begged for sheep and horses, wished to borrow troops to recover their old lands, and also asked to borrow Tiande fortress to lodge the princess—the emperor did not permit this.
translations.idiomatic: The Uighurs were then at their limit. They repeatedly begged for sheep and horses, wished to borrow troops to recover their old lands, and also asked to borrow Tiande fortress to lodge the princess—the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 乃進逼振武保大柵杷頭峰，以略朔川，轉戰雲州，刺史張獻節嬰城不出。

translations.literal: They then advanced and pressed Zhenwu's Baoda garrison at Patou Peak, raided Shuochuan, fought at Yunzhou—Prefect Zhang Xianjie held the city and would not come out.
translations.idiomatic: They then pressed Zhenwu's Baoda garrison at Patou Peak, raided Shuochuan, and fought as far as Yunzhou, where Prefect Zhang Xianjie held the city and would not come out.

sentences.zh: 回鶻乃大掠，党項、退渾皆保險莫敢拒。

translations.literal: The Uighurs then plundered on a great scale; Tangut and Tuyuhun all held the passes and dared not resist.
translations.idiomatic: The Uighurs then plundered on a great scale. The Tangut and Tuyuhun held their mountain strongholds and dared not resist.

sentences.zh: 帝益知向不許田牟用二部兵之效，乃復問以計，德裕曰：「杷頭峰北皆大磧，利用騎，不可以步當之。

translations.literal: The emperor all the more knew the effect of not having permitted Tian Mu to use the two tribes' troops; he again asked for a plan. Deyu said: "North of Patou Peak are all great deserts—advantage lies with cavalry; infantry cannot confront them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor all the more saw the wisdom of refusing Tian Mu's request for tribal troops and asked Deyu for another plan. Deyu said: "North of Patou Peak lies open desert—cavalry holds the advantage there, and infantry cannot stand against it.

sentences.zh: 今烏介所恃，公主爾，得健將出奇奪還之，王師急擊，彼必走。

translations.literal: Now what Wujie relies on is nothing but the princess—obtain a brave general to strike by surprise and retake her, and when imperial troops press the attack, they will surely flee.
translations.idiomatic: Wujie relies on nothing but the princess. Send a brave general to strike by surprise and retake her, then press the attack with imperial troops—they will surely flee.

sentences.zh: 今銳將無易石雄者，請以籓渾勁卒與漢兵銜枚夜擊之，勢必得。

translations.literal: Now among sharp generals none surpasses Shi Xiong—I ask that elite Fan and Tuyuhun troops with Han soldiers, with gagged mouths, strike by night—they will surely succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Among our best generals none surpasses Shi Xiong. I ask that elite Tuyuhun troops and Han soldiers strike by night with muffled mouths—they will surely succeed.

sentences.zh: 」帝即以方略授劉沔，令雄邀擊可汗于殺胡山，敗之，迎公主還，回鶻遂敗。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon entrusted the strategy to Liu Mian and ordered Xiong to intercept the khan at Shahu Mountain, defeated him, welcomed the princess back, and the Uighurs were thus defeated.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor thereupon entrusted the plan to Liu Mian and ordered Xiong to intercept the khan at Shahu Mountain. Xiong defeated him, brought the princess back, and the Uighurs were broken.

sentences.zh: 進位司徒。

translations.literal: Deyu was promoted to Minister over the Masses.
translations.idiomatic: Li Deyu was promoted to Minister over the Masses.

sentences.zh: 黠戛斯遣使來，且言攻取安西、北庭，帝欲從黠戛斯求其地，德裕曰：「不可。

translations.literal: The Kirghiz sent envoys, saying they had captured Anxi and Beiting; the emperor wished to seek those territories from the Kirghiz. Deyu said: "This cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: The Kirghiz sent envoys, reporting that they had captured Anxi and Beiting. The emperor wished to recover those territories through the Kirghiz. Deyu said: "This cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 安西距京師七千里，北庭五千里。

translations.literal: Anxi is seven thousand li from the capital, Beiting five thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Anxi lies seven thousand li from the capital, Beiting five thousand li.

sentences.zh: 異時繇河西、隴右抵玉門關，皆我郡縣，往往有兵，故能緩急調發。

translations.literal: In former times via Hexi and Longyou to Yumen Pass—all were our commanderies and counties, with troops stationed throughout, so forces could be mobilized for emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: In former times the route from Hexi and Longyou to Yumen Pass passed through our own commanderies and counties, with troops stationed all along the way, so forces could be mobilized in emergencies.

sentences.zh: 自河、隴入吐蕃，則道出回鶻。

translations.literal: From the Yellow River and Longyou into Tibet, the route passes through Uighur territory.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yellow River region and Longyou into Tibet, the route now passes through what was Uighur territory.

sentences.zh: 回鶻今破滅，未知黠戛斯果有其地邪？

translations.literal: The Uighurs are now destroyed—who knows whether the Kirghiz truly hold those lands?
translations.idiomatic: The Uighurs are now destroyed—who knows whether the Kirghiz truly hold those lands?

sentences.zh: 假令安西可得，即復置都護，以萬人往戍，何所興發，何道饋輓？

translations.literal: Even supposing Anxi could be recovered and the Protectorate re-established, to garrison it with ten thousand men—from where would they be raised, and by what route would supplies be transported?
translations.idiomatic: Even if Anxi could be recovered and the Protectorate restored, garrisoning it would take ten thousand men—from where would they be raised, and along what route would supplies be transported?

sentences.zh: 彼天德、振武于京師近，力猶苦不足，況七千里安西哉？

translations.literal: Tiande and Zhenwu, though near the capital, still find their strength insufficient—how much less seven-thousand-li Anxi?
translations.idiomatic: Tiande and Zhenwu, though close to the capital, already strain our resources—how much less seven-thousand-li Anxi?

sentences.zh: 臣以為縱得之，無用也。

translations.literal: Your subject believes that even if obtained, it would be of no use.
translations.idiomatic: I believe that even if we obtained it, it would be of no use.

sentences.zh: 昔漢魏相請罷田車師，賈捐之請棄珠崖，近狄仁傑亦請棄四鎮及安東，皆不願貪外以耗內。

translations.literal: Formerly in Han Wei Xiang asked to abandon farming at Jushi; Jia Juanzhi asked to abandon Zhuya; recently Di Renjie also asked to abandon the Four Garrisons and Andong—all unwilling to grasp the outer at the cost of exhausting the inner.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times Wei Xiang asked to abandon the Jushi garrison; Jia Juanzhi asked to abandon Zhuya; and more recently Di Renjie asked to abandon the Four Garrisons and Andong—all unwilling to grasp distant territories at the cost of draining the core.

sentences.zh: 此三臣者，當全盛時，尚欲棄割以肥中國，況久沒甚遠之地乎？

translations.literal: These three ministers, in times of full strength, still wished to abandon and cut away to enrich China—how much less lands long lost and extremely distant?
translations.idiomatic: These three ministers, even at the height of imperial power, still wished to abandon distant holdings to strengthen China itself—how much less territories lost long ago and impossibly far away?

sentences.zh: 是持實費，市虛事，滅一回鶻，而又生之。

translations.literal: This is to spend real expense to purchase empty show—to destroy one Uighur and create another.
translations.idiomatic: This would mean spending real treasure to buy an empty name—destroying one Uighur threat only to create another.

sentences.zh: 」帝乃止。

translations.literal: " The emperor then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then abandoned the idea.

sentences.zh: 澤潞劉從諫死，其從子稹擅留事，以邀節度，德裕曰：「澤潞內地，非河朔比，昔皆儒術大臣守之。

translations.literal: Liu Congjian of Zelu died; his nephew Zhi seized control of affairs to demand the military governorship. Deyu said: "Zelu is heartland territory—not comparable to Hebei and Shandong; formerly it was always held by Confucian scholar-officials.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Congjian of Zelu died, his nephew Zhi seized control of affairs to demand the military governorship. Deyu said: "Zelu lies in the heartland—not like Hebei and Shandong. In the past it was always held by Confucian scholar-officials.

sentences.zh: 李抱真始建昭義軍，最有功，德宗尚不許其子繼。

translations.literal: Li Baozhen first established the Zhaoyi Army with the greatest merit, yet Dezong still did not permit his son to succeed him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Baozhen, who first established the Zhaoyi Army, had rendered the greatest service, yet even Emperor Dezong would not let his son succeed him.

sentences.zh: 及劉悟死，敬宗方怠於政，遂以符節付從諫。

translations.literal: When Liu Wu died, Emperor Jingzong was just neglecting governance, and thus entrusted the insignia of command to Congjian.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Wu died, Emperor Jingzong was neglecting governance and thus entrusted the insignia of command to Congjian.

sentences.zh: 太和時，擅兵長子，陰連訓、注，外托效忠，請除君側。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he kept troops for his eldest son, secretly allied with Xun and Zhu, outwardly claiming loyalty and asking to remove enemies at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era he kept troops for his eldest son, secretly allied with Xun and Zhu, outwardly claiming loyalty while asking to remove enemies at the emperor's side.

sentences.zh: 及有狗馬疾，謝醫拒使，便以兵屬稹。

translations.literal: When he fell ill, he declined physicians and refused envoys, and transferred the troops to Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, he declined physicians and refused imperial envoys, then transferred command to Zhi.

sentences.zh: 舍而不討，無以示四方。

translations.literal: If let go without punishment, there will be no way to show the four quarters.
translations.idiomatic: If we let this pass unpunished, we will have no way to show our authority to the realm.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「可勝乎？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Can he be defeated?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor asked: "Can he be defeated?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「河朔，稹所恃以脣齒也。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Hebei and Shandong are what Zhi relies on as lips and teeth.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "Hebei and Shandong are the lips and teeth on which Zhi relies.

sentences.zh: 如令魏、鎮不與，則破矣。

translations.literal: If Wei and Zhen are made not to join him, he will be broken.
translations.idiomatic: If we ensure Wei and Zhen do not join him, he can be broken.

sentences.zh: 夫三鎮世嗣，列聖許之。

translations.literal: The three garrisons have hereditary succession—the successive emperors permitted this.
translations.idiomatic: The three garrisons have enjoyed hereditary succession—the successive emperors permitted this.

sentences.zh: 請使近臣明告：'以澤潞命帥，不得視三鎮，今朕欲誅稹，其各以兵會。

translations.literal: I ask that a close minister clearly announce: 'To appoint a commander for Zelu is not to be regarded like the three garrisons; now I wish to execute Zhi—each of you bring your troops to assemble.
translations.idiomatic: Send a close minister to announce clearly: 'Appointing a new commander for Zelu is not to be treated like the three garrisons. Now I intend to execute Zhi—each of you is to bring your troops and join the campaign.

sentences.zh: '」帝然之。

translations.literal: '" The emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: '" The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 乃以李回持節諭王元逵、何弘敬，皆聽命。

translations.literal: Li Hui was then sent with insignia to instruct Wang Yuankui and He Hongjing—both obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hui was then sent with imperial credentials to instruct Wang Yuankui and He Hongjing, and both obeyed.

sentences.zh: 始議用兵，中外交章固爭，皆曰：「悟功高，不可絕其嗣。

translations.literal: When military action was first discussed, memorials from court and frontier insisted in opposition, all saying: "Wu's merit was great—his line must not be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: When military action was first discussed, memorials from court and frontier alike insisted in opposition: "Liu Wu's merit was great—we must not cut off his line.

sentences.zh: 又從諫畜兵十萬，粟支十年，未可以破也。

translations.literal: Moreover Congjian stored a hundred thousand troops and grain to last ten years—it cannot be broken.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Congjian had stored a hundred thousand troops and grain for ten years—we cannot break him easily.

sentences.zh: 」它宰相亦媕婀趨和，德裕獨曰：「諸葛亮言曹操善為兵，猶五攻昌霸，三越漅，況其下哉？

translations.literal: " Other chief ministers also equivocated and chimed in; only Deyu said: "Zhuge Liang said that even Cao Cao, skilled in warfare, needed five attacks on Chang Ba and three crossings of Chao—how much less those below him?
translations.idiomatic: " The other chief ministers equivocated and chimed in. Only Deyu said: "Zhuge Liang observed that even Cao Cao, master of warfare, needed five attacks on Chang Ba and three crossings of Chao—how much less those below him?

sentences.zh: 然贏縮勝負，兵家之常，惟陛下聖策先定，不以小利鈍為浮議所搖，則有功矣。

translations.literal: Yet advance and retreat, victory and defeat—these are the constants of the art of war. Only if Your Majesty's sagacious plan is settled first and not dulled by petty gains or shaken by empty talk will there be achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Advance and retreat, victory and defeat—these are the constants of war. If Your Majesty settles on a firm plan and is not swayed by petty setbacks or empty talk, we will prevail.

sentences.zh: 有如不利，臣請以死塞責！

translations.literal: If there should be misfortune, your subject asks to meet death to fulfill his responsibility!
translations.idiomatic: If things go ill, I ask to meet death to answer for it!

sentences.zh: 」帝忿然曰：「為我語於朝，有沮吾軍議者，先誅之！

translations.literal: " The emperor said angrily: "Speak for me to the court—whoever obstructs my military deliberations, execute him first!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said angrily: "Tell the court for me: whoever obstructs my military plan shall be executed first!

sentences.zh: 」群論遂息。

translations.literal: " The clamor of opinion then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: " The chorus of dissent fell silent.

sentences.zh: 元逵兵已出，而弘敬逗留持兩端。

translations.literal: Yuankui's troops had already marched out, but Hongjing delayed and held to both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankui's troops had already marched, but Hongjing lingered, playing both sides.

sentences.zh: 德裕建遣王宰以陳、許精甲，假道于魏以伐磁。

translations.literal: Deyu proposed sending Wang Zai with elite troops from Chen and Xu, taking passage through Wei to attack Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu proposed sending Wang Zai with elite troops from Chen and Xu through Wei territory to attack Ci.

sentences.zh: 弘敬聞，遽勒兵請自涉漳取磁、潞。

translations.literal: When Hongjing heard this, he hastily mustered troops and asked to cross the Zhang himself to take Ci and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongjing heard this, he hastily mustered troops and volunteered to cross the Zhang River himself to take Ci and Lu.

sentences.zh: 會橫水戍兵叛，入太原，逐其帥李石，奉裨將楊弁主留事。

translations.literal: At the same time soldiers of the Hengshui garrison rebelled, entered Taiyuan, drove out their commander Li Shi, and installed the deputy general Yang Bian to manage affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time soldiers of the Hengshui garrison rebelled, entered Taiyuan, drove out their commander Li Shi, and installed Deputy General Yang Bian to manage affairs.

sentences.zh: 方是時，稹未下，朝廷益為憂。

translations.literal: At that time Zhi had not yet fallen, and the court grew more anxious.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhi had not yet fallen, and the court grew more anxious.

sentences.zh: 議者頗言兵皆可罷。

translations.literal: Those deliberating largely said the campaign should be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Many at court urged that the campaign be abandoned entirely.

sentences.zh: 帝遣中人馬元實如太原，偵其變。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched the eunuch Ma Yuanshi to Taiyuan to reconnoiter the revolt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched the eunuch Ma Yuanshi to Taiyuan to reconnoiter the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 弁厚賄中人，帳飲三日。

translations.literal: Bian lavishly bribed the eunuch and feasted in tent for three days.
translations.idiomatic: Bian lavishly bribed the eunuch and entertained him in his tent for three days.

sentences.zh: 還，謬曰：「弁兵多，屬明光甲者十五里。

translations.literal: On returning, he falsely reported: "Bian's troops are numerous—those wearing Bright Light armor stretch for fifteen li.
translations.idiomatic: On returning, he falsely reported: "Bian's troops are numerous—men in Bright Light armor stretch for fifteen li.

sentences.zh: 」德裕詰曰：「李石以太原無兵，故調橫水卒千五百使戍榆社，弁因以亂，渠能列卒如此多邪？

translations.literal: " Deyu questioned: "Li Shi, because Taiyuan had no troops, transferred fifteen hundred Hengshui soldiers to garrison Yushe; Bian rebelled from this—how could he array so many soldiers?
translations.idiomatic: " Deyu questioned: "Li Shi, because Taiyuan had no troops, transferred fifteen hundred Hengshui soldiers to garrison Yushe—that is how Bian came to rebel. How could he possibly array so many men?

sentences.zh: 」則曰：「晉人勇，皆兵也，募而得之。

translations.literal: " He then said: "The people of Jin are brave—all are soldiers, obtained by recruitment.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "The people of Jin are brave—all are soldiers, obtained by recruitment.

sentences.zh: 」德裕曰：「募士當以財，李石以人欠一縑，故兵亂，石無以索之，弁何得邪？

translations.literal: " Deyu said: "In recruiting soldiers one must use wealth. Li Shi had a man owing one bolt of silk, hence the military disorder. Shi had no way to collect it—how could Bian obtain them?"
translations.idiomatic: Deyu said: "Recruiting soldiers takes money. Li Shi had a man who owed one bolt of silk, and that is what sparked the mutiny. Shi had no way to collect the debt—how could Bian have raised an army?"

sentences.zh: 太原一鎧一戟，舉送行營，安致十五里明光乎？

translations.literal: One armor and one halberd from Taiyuan, all sent to the field camp—how could Bright Light armor stretch for fifteen li?
translations.idiomatic: Every piece of armor and every halberd in Taiyuan had been sent to the field camp—how could Bright Light armor possibly stretch for fifteen li?

sentences.zh: 」使者語塞。

translations.literal: " The envoy was left speechless.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy was left speechless.

sentences.zh: 德裕即奏：「弁賤伍，不可赦。

translations.literal: Deyu immediately memorialized: "Bian is a base enlisted man and must not be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu immediately memorialized: "Bian is a common soldier of no account. He must not be pardoned.

sentences.zh: 如力不足，請舍稹而誅弁。

translations.literal: If our strength is insufficient, I ask that we set aside Zhi and execute Bian.
translations.idiomatic: If our strength is insufficient, I ask that we set Zhi aside and execute Bian first.

sentences.zh: 」遽趣王逢起榆社軍，詔元逵趨土門，會太原。

translations.literal: " He immediately ordered Wang Feng to raise the Yushe troops, and commanded Yuankui to march to Tumen and converge on Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately ordered Wang Feng to raise the Yushe troops and commanded Yuankui to march on Tumen and rendezvous at Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 河東監軍呂義忠聞，即日召榆社卒入斬弁，獻首京師。

translations.literal: Lü Yizhong, military commissioner of Hedong, heard this and the same day summoned Yushe soldiers to enter and behead Bian, presenting the head in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Yizhong, military commissioner of Hedong, heard this, he that same day summoned the Yushe troops, had them enter Taiyuan and behead Bian, and sent the head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 德裕每疾貞元、太和間有所討伐，諸道兵出境，即仰給度支，多遷延以困國力。

translations.literal: Deyu always resented that during the Zhenyuan and Taihe periods, whenever campaigns were launched, troops of the various circuits upon leaving their borders relied on the Bureau of Revenue for supplies, often deliberately delaying and thereby straining the state's resources.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu had long resented that during the Zhenyuan and Taihe periods, whenever campaigns were launched, troops from the various circuits relied on the Bureau of Revenue for supplies as soon as they crossed their borders, often dragging out the fighting deliberately and thereby exhausting the state.

sentences.zh: 或與賊約，令懈守備，得一縣一屯以報天子，故師無大功。

translations.literal: Some would even conspire with the rebels, making them lax in defense, then take one county or one garrison to report to the Son of Heaven—thus the armies achieved no great victories.
translations.idiomatic: Some commanders even conspired with the rebels, inducing them to relax their defenses, then seized a single county or garrison to report to the emperor—so the armies won no decisive victories.

sentences.zh: 因請敕諸將，令直取州，勿攻縣。

translations.literal: He therefore requested an edict to the generals ordering them to strike directly for the prefectures and not attack counties.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore requested an edict ordering the generals to strike directly at the prefecture capitals and not waste time attacking counties.

sentences.zh: 故元逵等下邢、洺、磁，而稹氣索矣。

translations.literal: Accordingly Yuankui and the others took Xing, Ming, and Ci, and Zhi's spirit was exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly Yuankui and the others captured Xing, Ming, and Ci, and Zhi's will to fight collapsed.

sentences.zh: 俄而高文端歸命，稱稹糧乏，皆女子挼穟哺兵。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Gao Wenduan surrendered, reporting that Zhi's grain was depleted and women were threshing ears of grain by hand to feed the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Gao Wenduan surrendered, reporting that Zhi's grain stores were exhausted and women were threshing grain by hand to feed the soldiers.

sentences.zh: 未幾，郭誼持稹首降。

translations.literal: Before long, Guo Yi came bearing Zhi's head to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Guo Yi arrived bearing Liu Zhi's head to surrender.

sentences.zh: 帝問：「何以處誼？

translations.literal: The emperor asked: "How should Yi be treated?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "What should be done with Guo Yi?

sentences.zh: 」德裕曰：「稹豎子，安知反？

translations.literal: " Deyu said: "Zhi was a mere stripling—how could he know rebellion?
translations.idiomatic: Deyu said: "Zhi was a mere boy—what did he know of rebellion?

sentences.zh: 職誼為之。

translations.literal: It was Yi who did it.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Yi was the one who did it.

sentences.zh: 今三州已降，而稹窮蹙，又販其族以邀富貴，不誅，後無以懲惡。

translations.literal: Now three prefectures have surrendered, yet Zhi was cornered and Yi has sold out his own clan to seek wealth and rank—if not executed, there will be no deterring evil hereafter.
translations.idiomatic: Now three prefectures have surrendered, Zhi was cornered, and Yi sold out his own clan to buy wealth and rank. If he is not executed, there will be no deterring villainy in the future.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「朕意亦爾。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "My mind is likewise.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I think the same.

sentences.zh: 」因詔石雄入潞，盡取誼等及嘗為稹用者，悉誅之。

translations.literal: " Accordingly he ordered Shi Xiong to enter Lu, seize Yi and all who had served Zhi, and execute them all.
translations.idiomatic: He accordingly ordered Shi Xiong to enter Lu, arrest Guo Yi and everyone who had served Liu Zhi, and execute them all.

sentences.zh: 策功拜太尉，進封趙國公。

translations.literal: For his achievement in the strategy he was appointed Grand Preceptor and advanced to Duke of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: For his strategic achievement he was appointed Grand Preceptor and advanced to Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 德裕固讓，言：「唐興，太尉惟七人，尚父子儀乃不敢拜。

translations.literal: Deyu firmly declined, saying: "Since Tang arose, only seven men have been Grand Preceptor—even the heir of Prince Shang of Fu, Ziyu, did not dare accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu firmly declined, saying: "Since the founding of Tang, only seven men have been appointed Grand Preceptor—even Prince Shang's heir Ziyu did not dare accept the post.

sentences.zh: 近王智興、李載義皆超拜保、傅，蓋重惜此官。

translations.literal: Recently Wang Zhixing and Li Zaiyi were both abruptly promoted to Defender and Mentor—because this office is greatly cherished.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Wang Zhixing and Li Zaiyi were both abruptly promoted to Defender and Tutor of the Heir Apparent—because this office is regarded with great reverence.

sentences.zh: 裴度為司徒十年，亦不遷，臣願守舊秩足矣。

translations.literal: Pei Du served as Minister over the Masses for ten years without promotion. I wish only to keep my former rank, and that is enough.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Du served as Minister over the Masses for ten years without promotion. I would be satisfied to keep my present rank.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「吾恨無官酬公，毋固辭。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "I regret that I have no office with which to reward you—do not firmly decline.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "I regret that I have no higher office with which to reward you. Do not refuse again.

sentences.zh: 」德裕又陳：「先臣封于趙，塚孫寬中始生，字曰三趙，意將傳嫡，不及支庶。

translations.literal: " Deyu further submitted: "My deceased predecessor was enfeoffed in Zhao. When his tomb-inheritor Kuanzhong was born, his courtesy name was Sanzhao—his intention was to transmit it to the direct line and not to collateral branches.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu further submitted: "My ancestor was enfeoffed in Zhao. When his direct descendant Kuanzhong was born, he was given the courtesy name Sanzhao—meaning the title would pass only to the direct line, not to collateral branches.

sentences.zh: 臣前益封，已改中山。

translations.literal: When I was previously granted an additional enfeoffment, it was already changed to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: When I previously received an additional enfeoffment, it was already changed to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 臣先世皆嘗居汲，願得封衛。

translations.literal: My ancestors all once lived in Ji—I wish to be enfeoffed in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: My ancestors all once lived in Ji. I ask to be enfeoffed in Wei instead.

sentences.zh: 」從之，遂改衛國公。

translations.literal: " The emperor assented, and he was accordingly made Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented, and Deyu was accordingly made Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗從容謂宰相曰：「有人稱孔子其徒三千亦為黨，信乎？

translations.literal: The emperor once said at leisure to the chief ministers: "Some say that Confucius's three thousand disciples formed a faction—is it true?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said casually to the chief ministers: "Some say that Confucius's three thousand disciples formed a faction. Is that true?

sentences.zh: 」德裕曰：「昔劉向云：'孔子與顏回、子貢更相稱譽，不為朋黨；

translations.literal: " Deyu said: "Formerly Liu Xiang said: 'Confucius and Yan Hui and Zigong repeatedly praised one another, yet formed no faction;
translations.idiomatic: Deyu said: "Liu Xiang once wrote: 'Confucius and his disciples Yan Hui and Zigong praised one another in turn, yet did not form a faction;

sentences.zh: 禹、稷與皋陶轉相汲引，不為比周。

translations.literal: Yu and Ji and Gaoyao in turn recommended one another, yet did not form cliques.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, Ji, and Gaoyao recommended one another in turn, yet did not form cliques.

sentences.zh: 無邪心也。

translations.literal: There was no subversive intent.
translations.idiomatic: Their hearts were free of subversive intent.

sentences.zh: '臣嘗以共、鮌、驩兜與舜、禹雜處堯朝，共工、驩兜則為黨，舜、禹不為黨。

translations.literal: ' I once compared Gun, Gonggong, and Huandou with Shun and Yu, all mixed together in Yao's court—Gonggong and Huandou formed factions, while Shun and Yu did not.
translations.idiomatic: I have compared Gun, Gonggong, and Huandou with Shun and Yu, all serving together in Yao's court—Gonggong and Huandou formed factions, while Shun and Yu did not.

sentences.zh: 小人相與比周，迭為掩蔽也。

translations.literal: Petty men band together in cliques, alternately concealing one another's faults.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men band together in cliques, each covering for the other in turn.

sentences.zh: 賢人君子不然，忠於國則同心，聞于義則同志，退而各行其己，不可交以私。

translations.literal: Worthy men and gentlemen are not so—loyal to the state they share one heart, hearing what is right they share one purpose; when withdrawn each follows his own way and cannot be joined through private interest.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy men and gentlemen are not like that. Loyal to the state, they share one heart; hearing what is right, they share one purpose. In private each follows his own path, and cannot be bound together by personal interest.

sentences.zh: 趙宣子、隨會繼而納諫，司馬侯、叔向比以事君，不為黨也。

translations.literal: Zhao Xuanshi and Sui Hui in succession presented remonstrances; Sima Hou and Shu Xiang were close in serving their lord—they did not form a faction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xuanshi and Sui Hui in succession presented remonstrances; Sima Hou and Shu Xiang were close in serving their lord—they did not form a faction.

sentences.zh: 公孫弘每與汲黯請間，黯先發之，弘推其後，武帝所言皆聽。

translations.literal: Gongsun Hong often requested private audience with Ji An alongside him—Ji An would speak first, Hong would defer to him afterward, and Emperor Wu accepted all their counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Hong often requested private audience with Ji An—Ji An would speak first, Hong would follow, and Emperor Wu accepted all they said.

sentences.zh: 黯、弘雖並進，然廷詰齊人少情，譏其布被為詐，則先發後繼，不為黨也。

translations.literal: Although Ji and Hong both advanced in office, when in court Ji An denounced the man of Qi for lacking feeling and mocked his cotton quilt as deception, it was one speaking first and the other following after—not forming a faction.
translations.idiomatic: Although Ji and Hong both rose in office, when Ji An denounced a man of Qi for heartlessness and mocked his cotton quilt as a deception, one spoke first and the other followed—not forming a faction.

sentences.zh: 太宗與房玄齡圖事，則曰非杜如晦莫能籌之。

translations.literal: When Taizong consulted with Fang Xuanling on affairs, the latter would say that none but Du Ruhui could plan them.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong consulted with Fang Xuanling on affairs of state, Fang would say that only Du Ruhui could devise a plan.

sentences.zh: 及如晦在焉，亦推玄齡之策。

translations.literal: When Ruhui was present, he in turn deferred to Xuanling's strategies.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruhui was present, he would defer to Xuanling's strategies.

sentences.zh: 則同心圖國，不為黨也。

translations.literal: Thus they shared one heart in planning for the state—they did not form a faction.
translations.idiomatic: They shared one heart in planning for the state—they did not form a faction.

sentences.zh: 漢硃博、陳鹹相為腹心，背公死黨。

translations.literal: In Han, Zhu Bo and Chen Xian were each other's bosom allies, betraying the public and dying for their faction.
translations.idiomatic: In Han, Zhu Bo and Chen Xian were bosom allies who betrayed the public and died for their faction.

sentences.zh: 周福、房植各以其黨相傾，議論相軋，故朋黨始于甘陵二部。

translations.literal: Zhou Fu and Fang Zhi each used his faction to undermine the other, their opinions colliding in opposition—thus factions began with the two factions of Ganling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Fu and Fang Zhi each used his faction to undermine the other, their opinions clashing—thus factionalism began with the two factions of Ganling.

sentences.zh: 及甚也，謂之鉤黨，繼受誅夷。

translations.literal: When it reached its worst they were called the Hooked Faction, and subsequently suffered execution and extermination.
translations.idiomatic: When it reached its worst they were called the Hooked Faction, and subsequently suffered execution and extermination.

sentences.zh: 以王制言之，非不幸也。

translations.literal: Speaking by the royal institutions, this was no misfortune.
translations.idiomatic: By the standards of royal governance, this was no misfortune at all.

sentences.zh: 周之衰，列國公子有信陵、平原、孟嘗、春申，游談者以四豪為稱首，亦各有客三千，務以譎詐勢利相高；

translations.literal: When Zhou declined, the scions of the various states included Lord Xinling, Lord Pingyuan, Lord Mengchang, and Lord Chunshen; wandering persuaders hailed the Four Heroes as foremost, each also having three thousand retainers, striving to outdo one another in cunning and factional power;
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou declined, the scions of the various states included Lord Xinling, Lord Pingyuan, Lord Mengchang, and Lord Chunshen; wandering persuaders hailed the Four Heroes as foremost, each also keeping three thousand retainers, striving to outdo one another in cunning and the pursuit of power;

sentences.zh: 仲尼之徒，唯行仁義。

translations.literal: The followers of Zhongni practiced only benevolence and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: The followers of Confucius practiced only benevolence and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 今議者欲以比之，罔矣。

translations.literal: Those who now argue wish to compare them—and they are deceived.
translations.idiomatic: For those who now argue to compare the two is sheer delusion.

sentences.zh: 臣未知所謂黨者，為國乎？

translations.literal: Your subject does not know whether the so-called faction acts for the state—or not?
translations.idiomatic: I do not know whether the so-called factions serve the state—

sentences.zh: 為身乎？

translations.literal: Or for themselves?
translations.idiomatic: or for themselves?

sentences.zh: 誠為國邪，隨會、叔向、汲黯、房、杜之道可行，不必黨也。

translations.literal: If truly for the state, the way of Sui, Shu, Ji An, Fang, and Du may be followed—there is no need for faction.
translations.idiomatic: If they truly serve the state, then the way of Sui Hui, Shu Xiang, Ji An, Fang Xuanling, and Du Ruhui may be followed—without forming factions at all.

sentences.zh: 今所謂黨者，誣善蔽忠，附下罔上，車馬馳驅，以趨權勢，晝夜合謀，美官要選，悉引其黨為之，否則抑壓以退。

translations.literal: The so-called factions of today slander the good and conceal the loyal, attach themselves to subordinates and deceive superiors, race chariots and horses to seek power, plot together day and night, and for fine offices and key posts all install their faction members—otherwise they suppress and force one to withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: The so-called factions of today slander the good and conceal the loyal, attach themselves to subordinates and deceive superiors, race to the seats of power, plot together day and night, and install their own men in every fine office and key post—or else suppress rivals and force them out.

sentences.zh: 仲尼之徒，有是乎？

translations.literal: Did the followers of Zhongni do such things?
translations.idiomatic: Did the followers of Confucius ever behave like this?

sentences.zh: 陛下以是察之，則奸偽見矣。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty examines by this standard, deceit and falsity will be revealed.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty examines them by this standard, deceit and falsity will stand revealed.

sentences.zh: 時韋弘質建言：「宰相不可兼治錢穀。

translations.literal: At that time Wei Hongzhi submitted a proposal: "Chief ministers should not concurrently administer finances and grain.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wei Hongzhi submitted a proposal: "Chief ministers should not concurrently administer finances and grain.

sentences.zh: 」德裕奏言：「管仲明于治國，其語曰：'國之重器，莫重於令。

translations.literal: " Deyu memorialized: "Guan Zhong was enlightened in governing the state. He said: 'The state's weightiest instrument—nothing is weightier than the command.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu memorialized: "Guan Zhong understood governance. He said: 'Of the state's weightiest instruments, none is weightier than the command.

sentences.zh: 令重君尊，君尊國安。

translations.literal: When commands are weighty the lord is revered; when the lord is revered the state is secure.
translations.idiomatic: When commands carry weight the ruler is revered; when the ruler is revered the state is secure.

sentences.zh: 治人之本，莫要於令。

translations.literal: The root of governing men—nothing is more essential than the command.
translations.idiomatic: The root of governing men—nothing is more essential than the command.

sentences.zh: '故曰'虧令者死，益令者死，不行令者死，留令者死，不從令者死。

translations.literal: ' Therefore it is said: "He who diminishes the command dies; he who augments the command dies; he who does not execute the command dies; he who withholds the command dies; he who does not obey the command dies.
translations.idiomatic: ' Hence it is said: "He who diminishes the command shall die; he who augments the command shall die; he who fails to execute the command shall die; he who withholds the command shall die; he who disobeys the command shall die.

sentences.zh: 五者無赦。

translations.literal: For these five there is no pardon.
translations.idiomatic: For these five offenses there is no pardon.

sentences.zh: '又曰：'令在上而論可否在下，是主威下系於人也。

translations.literal: ' He also said: 'When commands come from above but below they debate whether they are feasible, then the ruler's authority is bound to other men below.
translations.idiomatic: ' He also said: 'When commands come from above but subordinates below debate their feasibility, the ruler's authority is bound to other men.

sentences.zh: '太和後，風俗浸敝，令出於上，非之在下。

translations.literal: ' After the Taihe era customs gradually decayed—commands issued from above, but below they were rejected.
translations.idiomatic: ' After the Taihe era customs gradually decayed—commands issued from above were rejected below.

sentences.zh: 此敝不止，無以治國。

translations.literal: If this decay does not stop, the state cannot be governed.
translations.idiomatic: If this decay is not stopped, the state cannot be governed.

sentences.zh: 匡衡曰：'大臣者，國家股肱，萬姓所瞻仰，明主所慎擇也。

translations.literal: Kuang Heng said: 'Grand ministers are the state's arms and legs, whom the myriad people look up to—carefully chosen by an enlightened lord.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang Heng said: 'Grand ministers are the arms and legs of the state, whom the common people look up to—carefully chosen by a wise ruler.

sentences.zh: '《傳》曰：'下輕其上爵，賤人圖柄臣，則國家搖動而人不靜。

translations.literal: ' The Classic of History says: 'When inferiors hold the noble ranks above them lightly and base men plot against the ministers of power, then the state is shaken and the people are unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: ' The Classic of History says: 'When inferiors hold the nobility in contempt and base men plot against the ministers of power, then the state is shaken and the people are unsettled.

sentences.zh: '今弘質為人所教而言，是圖柄臣者也。

translations.literal: ' Now Hongzhi speaks as one instructed by others—this is plotting against the ministers of power.
translations.idiomatic: ' Hongzhi speaks as one instructed by others—this is plotting against the ministers of power.

sentences.zh: 且蕭望之，漢名儒，為御史大夫，奏云：'歲首，日月少光，咎在臣等。

translations.literal: Moreover Xiao Wangzhi, a famous Han scholar, served as Censor-in-Chief and memorialized: 'At the year's beginning the sun and moon shone dimly—the fault lies with your ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Xiao Wangzhi, a famous Han scholar, served as Censor-in-Chief and memorialized: 'At the year's beginning the sun and moon shone dimly—the fault lies with us, your ministers.

sentences.zh: '宣帝以望之意輕丞相，下有司詰問。

translations.literal: ' Emperor Xuan, believing Wangzhi slighted the chief minister, ordered the relevant offices to investigate and question him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan, believing Wangzhi was slighting the chief minister, ordered the relevant offices to investigate and question him.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，監察御史陳師合上言：'人之思慮有限，一人不可總數職。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era, Supervising Censor Chen Shihe submitted a memorial: 'Men's deliberations are limited—one man cannot oversee several offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan era, Supervising Censor Chen Shihe submitted a memorial: 'Men's capacity for deliberation is limited—one man cannot oversee several offices at once.

sentences.zh: '太宗曰：'此欲離間我君臣。

translations.literal: ' Taizong said: 'This is meant to drive a wedge between sovereign and minister.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said: 'This is meant to drive a wedge between sovereign and minister.

sentences.zh: '斥之嶺外。

translations.literal: ' He banished him beyond the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong banished him beyond the mountains.

sentences.zh: 臣謂宰相有奸謀隱慝，則人人皆得上論。

translations.literal: Your subject holds that if chief ministers harbor treacherous designs and hidden wrongdoing, then every man may submit criticism from below.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that if chief ministers harbor treacherous designs and hidden wrongdoing, then every man may submit criticism.

sentences.zh: 至於制置職業，人主之柄，非小人所得幹。

translations.literal: As for arranging offices and duties—that is the sovereign's prerogative, not something petty men may meddle in.
translations.idiomatic: As for arranging offices and duties—that is the sovereign's prerogative, not something petty men may meddle in.

sentences.zh: 古者朝廷之士，各守官業，思不出位。

translations.literal: In antiquity court gentlemen each kept to his official duties and did not let his thoughts go beyond his station.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity court gentlemen each kept to his official duties and did not let his thoughts stray beyond his station.

sentences.zh: 弘質賤臣，豈得以非所宜言妄觸天聽！

translations.literal: Hongzhi is a base official—how can he speak what is not his place to say and rashly reach the imperial ear!
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi is a base official—how can he speak of what is not his place to speak of and rashly reach the imperial ear!

sentences.zh: 是輕宰相。

translations.literal: This is to hold the chief minister lightly.
translations.idiomatic: This is to hold the chief minister in contempt.

sentences.zh: 陛下照其邪計，從党人中來，當遏絕之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should perceive his treacherous scheme, coming from among the faction members, and cut it off.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should see that this treacherous scheme comes from the faction members and cut it off.

sentences.zh: 」德裕大意，欲朝廷尊，臣下肅，而政出宰相，深疾朋黨，故感憤切言之。

translations.literal: " Deyu's general intent was that the court be revered, the subjects be solemn, and government proceed from the chief ministers; he deeply hated factions, and so spoke with indignant urgency.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu's general intent was that the court should be revered, ministers should be disciplined, and government should proceed from the chief ministers. He deeply hated factions, and so spoke with indignant urgency.

sentences.zh: 又嘗謂：「省事不如省官，省官不如省吏，能簡冗官，誠治本也。

translations.literal: He also once said: "Cutting affairs is not as good as cutting offices; cutting offices is not as good as cutting clerks—being able to simplify redundant offices is truly treating the root.
translations.idiomatic: He also once said: "Cutting affairs is not as good as cutting offices; cutting offices is not as good as cutting clerks—to simplify redundant offices is truly to treat the root of the problem.

sentences.zh: 」乃請罷郡縣吏凡二千餘員，衣冠去者皆怨。

translations.literal: " He then requested the dismissal of more than two thousand county and district clerks; those who departed office resented it.
translations.idiomatic: He then requested the dismissal of more than two thousand county and district clerks. Those who lost their posts resented him deeply.

sentences.zh: 時天下已平，數上疏乞骸骨，而星家言熒惑犯上相，又懇丐去位，皆不許。

translations.literal: At that time the realm was already pacified; he repeatedly submitted memorials begging to retire, and when astrologers said Mars had encroached upon the senior minister, he again earnestly begged to leave office—all without permission.
translations.idiomatic: By then the realm was already pacified. He repeatedly submitted memorials begging to retire, and when astrologers reported that Mars had encroached upon the senior minister's star, he again earnestly begged to leave office—all without success.

sentences.zh: 當國凡六年，方用兵時，決策制勝，它相無與，故威名獨重于時。

translations.literal: He governed for six years in all; when military action was underway he made the decisions that secured victory, and no other chief minister shared in it—thus his prestige alone weighed heavily in the age.
translations.idiomatic: He governed for six years in all. During the military campaign he made every decision that secured victory, and no other chief minister shared in it—thus his prestige alone stood supreme in the age.

sentences.zh: 宣宗即位，德裕奉冊太極殿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuanzong ascended, Deyu presented the succession document in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuanzong ascended the throne, Deyu presented the succession document in the Hall of Supreme Ultimate.

sentences.zh: 帝退謂左右曰：「向行事近我者，非太尉邪？

translations.literal: The emperor withdrew and said to those beside him: "Was it not the Grand Preceptor who stood nearest me during the ceremony just now?
translations.idiomatic: After the ceremony the emperor said to those beside him: "Was it not the Grand Preceptor who stood nearest to me during the rites?

sentences.zh: 每顧我，毛髮為森豎。

translations.literal: Every time he looked at me my hair stood on end.
translations.idiomatic: Every time he looked at me my hair stood on end.

sentences.zh: 」翌日，罷為檢校司徒、同中書門下平章事，荊南節度使。

translations.literal: " The next day he was dismissed to serve as honorary Minister over the Masses and concurrent Grand Counsellor, military governor of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Deyu was dismissed to the post of honorary Minister over the Masses and concurrent Grand Counsellor, military governor of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 俄徙東都留守。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to be Protector of the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to be Protector of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 白敏中、令狐綯、崔鉉皆素仇，大中元年，使党人李鹹斥德裕陰事。

translations.literal: Bai Minzhong, Linghu Tao, and Cui Xuan were all old enemies; in the first year of Dazhong they had the faction member Li Xian denounce Deyu's hidden affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Minzhong, Linghu Tao, and Cui Xuan were all old enemies. In the first year of Dazhong they had the faction member Li Xian denounce Deyu's hidden affairs.

sentences.zh: 故以太子少保分司東都，再貶潮州司馬。

translations.literal: Accordingly he was made Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent with detached duty at the Eastern Capital, then demoted again to military adjutant of Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly he was made Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent with detached duty at the Eastern Capital, then demoted again to military adjutant of Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，又導吳汝納訟李紳殺吳湘事，而大理卿盧言、刑部侍郎馬植、御史中丞魏扶言：「紳殺無罪，德裕徇成其冤，至為黜御史，罔上不道。

translations.literal: The next year they also incited Wu Runa to sue over Li Shen's killing of Wu Xiang, and Minister of Justice Lu Yan, Vice Minister of Justice Ma Zhi, and Censor-in-Chief Wei Fu said: "Shen killed an innocent man; Deyu bent the law to confirm the injustice, even dismissing censors—deceiving the sovereign, a crime beyond measure.
translations.idiomatic: The next year they also incited Wu Runa to sue over Li Shen's killing of Wu Xiang. Minister of Justice Lu Yan, Vice Minister of Justice Ma Zhi, and Censor-in-Chief Wei Fu declared: "Shen killed an innocent man, and Deyu bent the law to confirm the injustice, even dismissing censors—deceiving the sovereign, a crime beyond measure.

sentences.zh: 」乃貶為崖州司戶參軍事。

translations.literal: " He was accordingly demoted to Clerk of the Revenue Section at Yazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu was accordingly demoted to Clerk of the Revenue Section at Yazhou.

sentences.zh: 明年，卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: The next year he died, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he died, aged sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 德裕既沒，見夢令狐綯曰：「公幸哀我，使得歸葬。

translations.literal: After Deyu's death he appeared in a dream to Linghu Tao, saying: "Sir, pity me and let me be returned for burial.
translations.idiomatic: After Deyu's death he appeared in a dream to Linghu Tao, saying: "Sir, have pity on me and let my body be returned for burial.

sentences.zh: 」綯語其子滈，滈曰：「執政皆共憾，可乎？

translations.literal: " Tao told his son Hao, and Hao said: "Those in power all share this resentment—can it be done?
translations.idiomatic: Tao told his son Hao, and Hao said: "Those in power all share this resentment—can we really do this?

sentences.zh: 」既夕，又夢，綯懼曰：「衛公精爽可畏，不言，禍將及。

translations.literal: " That evening he dreamed again; Tao feared and said: "The Duke of Wei's spirit is formidable—if I do not speak, calamity will come upon me.
translations.idiomatic: That evening he dreamed again. Tao said in fear: "The Duke of Wei's spirit is formidable—if I do not speak, calamity will come upon me.

sentences.zh: 」白於帝，得以喪還。

translations.literal: " He reported to the emperor, and the body was permitted to be returned.
translations.idiomatic: He reported to the emperor, and Deyu's body was permitted to be returned.

sentences.zh: 德裕性孤峭，明辯有風采，善為文章。

translations.literal: Deyu was by nature solitary and stern, clear in debate and possessed of presence, skilled in literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu was by nature solitary and stern, clear in debate and possessed of great presence, and skilled in literary composition.

sentences.zh: 雖至大位，猶不去書。

translations.literal: Even upon reaching the highest office he still did not put aside his books.
translations.idiomatic: Even upon reaching the highest office he still did not put aside his books.

sentences.zh: 其謀議援古為質，袞袞可喜。

translations.literal: In his counsel and deliberations he drew on antiquity for substance—flowing and admirable.
translations.idiomatic: In his counsel and deliberations he drew on antiquity for substance—his discourse flowed richly and was a delight to read.

sentences.zh: 常以經綸天下自為，武宗知而能任之，言從計行，是時王室幾中興。

translations.literal: He always took upon himself the task of governing the realm; Emperor Wuzong knew this and was able to employ him; his words were heeded and his plans carried out; at that time the royal house nearly achieved restoration.
translations.idiomatic: He always held himself responsible for governing the empire. Emperor Wuzong recognized this and put his full trust in him—every word was heeded, every plan executed. At that time the dynasty came near to a genuine revival.

sentences.zh: 先是，韓全義敗于蔡，杜叔良敗于深，皆監軍宦人制其權，將不得專進退，詔書一日三四下，宰相不豫。

translations.literal: Before this, Han Quanyi was defeated at Cai and Du Shuliang was defeated at Shen—in both cases eunuch army supervisors controlled authority; generals could not alone decide advance or retreat; imperial edicts went out three or four times a day; the chief ministers were not consulted.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Han Quanyi had been defeated at Cai and Du Shuliang at Shen—in both cases eunuch army supervisors held real authority. Generals could not move troops at their own discretion, and three or four imperial edicts might issue in a single day without the chief ministers being consulted.

sentences.zh: 又諸道銳兵票士，皆監軍取以自隨，每督戰，乘高建旗自表，師小不勝，輒卷旗去，大兵隨以北。

translations.literal: Moreover, the finest troops and fiercest warriors of the various circuits were taken by the army supervisors for their personal retinues. Whenever they directed battle, they would ride to high ground and raise their banners to display themselves; if the army met with even a small defeat they would immediately furl their banners and leave, and the main force would follow them in retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Furthermore, the best troops and fiercest warriors from every circuit were taken by army supervisors for their personal retinues. When they directed battle they would ride to high ground and raise their banners in display; at the slightest setback they would furl their banners and withdraw, and the main army would retreat with them.

sentences.zh: 繇是王師所向多負。

translations.literal: Thus the imperial army met defeat wherever it went.
translations.idiomatic: From this the imperial armies met defeat more often than not.

sentences.zh: 至討回鶻、澤潞，德裕建請詔書付宰司乃下，監軍不得幹軍要，率兵百人取一以為衛。

translations.literal: When it came to the campaigns against the Uyghurs and Ze-Lu, Deyu memorialized requesting that edicts be issued only after delivery to the chief ministers; army supervisors were not permitted to interfere in military essentials; for every hundred troops one was taken to serve as guard.
translations.idiomatic: When campaigns were launched against the Uyghurs and against Ze and Lu, Deyu proposed that no imperial edict issue until it had first passed through the chief ministers, that army supervisors be barred from meddling in military decisions, and that only one man per hundred in each unit serve as a guard detail.

sentences.zh: 自是，號令明壹，將乃有功。

translations.literal: From this time commands were clear and unified, and generals could achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: From that point on, orders were clear and uniform, and commanders were finally able to win real victories.

sentences.zh: 元和後數用兵，宰相不休沐，或繼火，乃得罷。

translations.literal: After the Yuanhe reign, when troops were repeatedly deployed, chief ministers did not take their days of rest; sometimes they worked through the night before they could cease.
translations.idiomatic: In the years after Yuanhe, whenever troops were mobilized, chief ministers went without their rest days—sometimes working by lamplight deep into the night before they could stand down.

sentences.zh: 德裕在位，雖遽書警奏，皆從容裁決，率午漏下還第，休沐輒如令，沛然若無事時。

translations.literal: While Deyu held office, even when urgent dispatches and alarming memorials arrived, he decided them at his ease; as a rule he returned home after the noon watch; on rest days he observed the regulations; his manner was serene as in a time of peace.
translations.idiomatic: While Deyu held office, even urgent dispatches and alarming reports were handled with unruffled ease. As a rule he returned home after the noon watch, took his scheduled days of rest without fail, and maintained a composure as tranquil as if the realm were entirely at peace.

sentences.zh: 其處報機急，帝一切令德裕作詔，德裕數辭，帝曰：「學士不能盡吾意。

translations.literal: When urgent reports arrived, the emperor ordered Deyu to draft all edicts in response. Deyu repeatedly declined. The emperor said: "The academicians cannot fully express my intent.
translations.idiomatic: When urgent reports arrived, the emperor ordered Deyu to draft every edict in response. Deyu repeatedly declined, but the emperor said, "The academicians cannot fully express what I mean.

sentences.zh: 」伐劉稹也，詔王元逵、何弘敬曰：「勿為子孫之謀，存輔車之勢。

translations.literal: " When the campaign against Liu Zhen was launched, an edict to Wang Yuankui and He Hongjing said: "Do not scheme for the sake of your descendants; preserve the mutual-support bond between us.
translations.idiomatic: " In the campaign against Liu Zhen, an edict to Wang Yuankui and He Hongjing read: "Do not scheme for your descendants' advantage; preserve the bond of mutual support between us.

sentences.zh: 」元逵等情得，皆震恐思效。

translations.literal: " Yuankui and the others understood the point; all were shaken with fear and resolved to exert themselves in service.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuankui and the others grasped the warning; all were shaken with fear and resolved to prove themselves in service.

sentences.zh: 已而三州降，賊遂平。

translations.literal: Before long three prefectures surrendered, and the rebels were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Before long three prefectures surrendered, and the rebellion was put down.

sentences.zh: 帝每稱魏博功，則顧德裕道詔語，咨其切於事而能伐謀也。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor praised the achievements of Weibo, he would turn to Deyu and repeat the wording of the edict, asking whether it had been apt to the situation and able to undercut stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor praised Weibo's achievements, he would turn to Deyu and repeat the edict's wording, asking whether it had been apt to the situation and able to forestall enemy stratagems.

sentences.zh: 三鎮每奏事，德裕引使者戒敕為忠義，指意丁寧，使歸各為其帥道之，故河朔畏威不敢慢。

translations.literal: Whenever the three circuits memorialized, Deyu would summon their envoys, admonish them with warnings of loyalty and righteousness, carefully convey his meaning, and send them back each to report to their own commanders. Thus the Hebei region feared his authority and dared not treat affairs lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the three circuits sent memorials, Deyu would summon their envoys, warn them to serve with loyalty and righteousness, carefully convey his meaning, and send them back to report to their own commanders. Thus the Hebei region feared his authority and dared not treat affairs lightly.

sentences.zh: 後除浮屠法，僧亡命多趣幽州，德裕召邸吏戒曰：「為我謝張仲武，劉從諫招納亡命，今視之何益？

translations.literal: Later, when the Buddhist monastic law was abolished, many monks fled toward Youzhou. Deyu summoned a lodging-house clerk and warned: "Convey my message to Zhang Zhongwu: Liu Congjian used to shelter fugitives—what good does it do to look at it that way now?
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Buddhist monastic law was abolished, many monks fled toward Youzhou. Deyu summoned a lodging-house clerk and warned, "Carry my message to Zhang Zhongwu: Liu Congjian once sheltered fugitives—what good does it do you to follow that example now?

sentences.zh: 」仲武懼，以刀授居庸關吏曰：「僧敢入者，斬！

translations.literal: " Zhongwu was alarmed. He gave a sword to the gate officer at Juyong Pass and said: "If any monk dares to enter, cut him down!
translations.idiomatic: " Zhongwu was alarmed. He gave a sword to the gate officer at Juyong Pass and said, "If any monk dares to enter, cut him down!

sentences.zh: 帝既數討叛有功，德裕慮忲于武，不可戢，即奏言：「曹操破袁紹於官渡，不追奔，自謂所獲已多，恐傷威重。

translations.literal: The emperor having repeatedly succeeded in suppressing rebellion, Deyu worried he was growing arrogant in military matters and could not be restrained. He submitted a memorial saying: "When Cao Cao defeated Yuan Shao at Guandu, he did not pursue the fugitives, saying to himself that his gains were already sufficient and fearing injury to his majesty and weight.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor having repeatedly succeeded in suppressing rebellion, Deyu worried that martial success was making him overbold and that he could no longer be restrained. He submitted a memorial saying, "When Cao Cao defeated Yuan Shao at Guandu, he did not pursue the fugitives, telling himself his gains were already sufficient and fearing to diminish his authority.

sentences.zh: 養由基古善射者，柳葉雖百步必中，觀者曰：'不如少息，若弓撥矢鉤，前功皆棄。

translations.literal: Yang Youji was an ancient master archer—though the target were willow leaves at a hundred paces he never missed. An onlooker said: 'Better to pause for a moment; if the bowstring slips or the arrow-hook catches, all your previous achievement will be lost.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Youji was an ancient master archer—though the target were willow leaves at a hundred paces he never missed. An onlooker said, 'Better pause for a moment; if the bowstring slips or the arrow-hook catches, all your previous achievement will be lost.

sentences.zh: '陛下征伐無不得所欲，願以兵為戒，乃可保成功。

translations.literal: 'Your Majesty has in every campaign obtained whatever you desired. I pray you take the use of arms as a warning—only then can success be preserved.
translations.idiomatic: 'Your Majesty has in every campaign obtained whatever you desired. I pray you take the use of arms as a warning—only then can success be preserved.

sentences.zh: 」帝嘉納其言。

translations.literal: " The emperor praised and accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor praised and accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 方士趙歸真以術進，德裕諫曰：「是嘗敬宗時以詭妄出入禁中，人皆不願至陛下前。

translations.literal: The adept Zhao Guizhen advanced through arts of the Way. Deyu remonstrated: "This man in Emperor Jingzong's time came and went in the forbidden precincts through deceit and falsehood—everyone wished he would not appear before Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: The adept Zhao Guizhen advanced through arts of the Way. Deyu remonstrated, "This man in Emperor Jingzong's time came and went in the forbidden precincts through deceit and falsehood—everyone wished he would not appear before Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「歸真我自識，顧無大過，召與語養生術爾。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "I know Guizhen myself; besides he has no serious fault. I summon him only to discuss techniques of nourishing life.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "I know Guizhen myself; besides, he has no serious fault. I summon him only to discuss techniques of nourishing life.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「小人於利，若蛾赴燭。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Petty men toward profit are like moths rushing into a flame.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied, "Petty men toward profit are like moths rushing into a flame.

sentences.zh: 向見歸真之門，車轍滿矣。

translations.literal: Just now I passed Guizhen's gate—the tracks of carriages already filled it.
translations.idiomatic: Just now I passed Guizhen's gate—the wheel ruts of carriages already filled the road before it.

sentences.zh: 」帝不聽。

translations.literal: " The emperor did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 於是挾術詭時者進，帝志衰焉。

translations.literal: From this, men who relied on arts and deceived the times advanced, and the emperor's resolve weakened.
translations.idiomatic: From this, men who trafficked in arts and deceived the times advanced, and the emperor's resolve waned.

sentences.zh: 所居安邑裏第，有院號「起草」，亭曰「精思」，每計大事，則處其中，雖左右侍御不得豫。

translations.literal: At his residence, the mansion in Anyi Lane, there was a courtyard called "Drafting" and a pavilion called "Refined Thought." Whenever he planned great affairs he sequestered himself within—none of his attendants, not even those at his side, were permitted to take part.
translations.idiomatic: At his residence, the mansion in Anyi Lane, there was a courtyard called "Drafting" and a pavilion called "Refined Thought." Whenever he planned great affairs he sequestered himself within—not even his closest attendants were permitted to take part.

sentences.zh: 不喜飲酒，後房無聲色娛。

translations.literal: He did not care for wine; in his inner quarters there was no music or beauty for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: He did not care for wine, and in his inner quarters there was no music or beauty for amusement.

sentences.zh: 生平所論著多行於世雲。

translations.literal: The treatises and writings of his lifetime mostly circulated in the world, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: The treatises and writings of his lifetime mostly circulated in the world, it is said.

sentences.zh: 子 燁子燁，仕汴宋幕府，貶象州立山尉。

translations.literal: Son: Ye. Ye served on the staff of Biansong and was demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Lishan in Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ye served on the staff of Biansong and was demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Lishan in Xiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 懿宗時，以赦令徙郴州。

translations.literal: During Emperor Yizong's reign, by amnesty edict he was transferred to Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Yizong's reign, by amnesty edict he was transferred to Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 餘子皆從死貶所。

translations.literal: His remaining sons all followed him to die in the place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: His remaining sons all followed him into exile and died there.

sentences.zh: 燁子 延吉燁子延吉，乾符中，為集賢校理，擢累司勳員外郎，還居平泉。

translations.literal: Ye's son Yenji. In the Qianfu reign he served as collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, rose through promotion to Vice Director of the Ministry of Honors, and returned to reside at Pingquan.
translations.idiomatic: Ye's son Yenji. In the Qianfu reign he served as collator at the Hall of Assembled Worthies, rose through promotion to Vice Director of the Ministry of Honors, and returned to live at Pingquan.

sentences.zh: 昭宗東遷，坐不朝謁，貶衛尉主簿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong moved east, for failing to attend court audience he was demoted to Senior Clerk of the Court of Imperial Regalia.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong moved east, for failing to attend court audience he was demoted to Senior Clerk of the Court of Imperial Regalia.

sentences.zh: 附 崔嘏 丁柔立德裕之斥，中書舍人崔嘏，字乾錫，誼士也。

translations.literal: Appendix: Cui Gu and Ding Rouli. When Deyu was driven out, Cui Gu, Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat, styled Qianxi, was a man of integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Appendix: Cui Gu and Ding Rouli. When Deyu was driven out, Cui Gu, Attendant Gentleman of the Secretariat, styled Qianxi, was a man of integrity.

sentences.zh: 坐書制不深切，貶端州刺史。

translations.literal: For composing an edict that was not trenchant enough, he was demoted to Prefect of Duan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For composing an edict that was not trenchant enough, he was demoted to Prefect of Duan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘏舉進士，復以制策曆刑州刺史。

translations.literal: Gu passed the jinshi examination and by decree examination successively served as Prefect of Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Gu passed the jinshi examination and, by decree examination, successively served as Prefect of Xing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 劉稹叛，使其党裴問戍於州，嘏說使聽命，改考功郎中，時皆謂遴賞。

translations.literal: When Liu Zhen rebelled, he sent his partisan Pei Wen to garrison the prefecture. Gu persuaded Wen to obey orders; he was reassigned as Director in the Ministry of Personnel. At the time all said the reward was carefully chosen.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Zhen rebelled, he sent his partisan Pei Wen to garrison the prefecture. Gu persuaded Wen to obey orders and was reassigned as Director in the Ministry of Personnel. At the time all said the reward was carefully chosen.

sentences.zh: 至是，作詔不肯巧傅以罪。

translations.literal: At this point, in drafting the edict he refused to artfully attach guilt.
translations.idiomatic: At this point, in drafting the edict he refused to artfully attach guilt to Deyu.

sentences.zh: 吳汝納之獄，朝廷公卿無為辨者，惟淮南府佐魏鉶就逮，吏使誣引德裕，雖痛楚掠，終不從，竟貶死嶺外。

translations.literal: In the case of Wu Runa, none of the nobles and chief ministers at court spoke in his defense. Only Wei Xing, an aide on the Huainan governor's staff, was taken into custody. The officers had him falsely implicate Deyu; though tortured and racked with pain, he never yielded, and in the end was demoted and died beyond the Ling Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: In the case of Wu Runa, none of the nobles and chief ministers at court spoke in his defense. Only Wei Xing, an aide on the Huainan governor's staff, was taken into custody. The officers had him falsely implicate Deyu; though tortured and racked with pain, he never yielded, and in the end was demoted and died beyond the Ling Mountains.

sentences.zh: 又丁柔立者，德裕當國時，或薦其直清可任諫爭官，不果用。

translations.literal: There was also Ding Rouli. While Deyu held state power, some recommended him as upright and pure, fit to serve as a remonstrating official, but he was not appointed.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Ding Rouli. While Deyu held state power, some recommended him as upright and pure, fit to serve as a remonstrating official, but he was not appointed.

sentences.zh: 大中初，為左拾遺。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Dazhong reign he served as Left Remonstrance Officer.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Dazhong reign he served as Left Remonstrance Officer.

sentences.zh: 既德裕被放，柔立內湣傷之，為上書直其冤，坐阿附，貶南陽尉。

translations.literal: After Deyu was banished, Rouli mourned him inwardly and submitted a memorial asserting his innocence. For partisanship he was demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Deyu was banished, Rouli mourned him inwardly and submitted a memorial asserting his innocence. For partisanship he was demoted to Assistant Magistrate of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 懿宗時，詔追復德裕太子少保、衛國公，贈尚書左僕射，距其沒十年。

translations.literal: During Emperor Yizong's reign, an edict posthumously restored Deyu to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Duke of Weiguo, and conferred upon him the post of Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs—ten years after his death.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Yizong's reign, an edict posthumously restored Deyu to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and Duke of Weiguo, and conferred upon him the post of Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs—ten years after his death.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：漢劉向論朋黨，其言明切，可為流涕，而主不悟，卒陷亡辜。

translations.literal: The commentator says: In Han, Liu Xiang's discourse on factions—his words were clear and piercing, enough to draw tears, yet the ruler did not understand; in the end innocent men were destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: In Han, Liu Xiang's discourse on factions—his words were clear and piercing, enough to draw tears, yet the ruler did not understand; in the end innocent men were destroyed.

sentences.zh: 德裕復援向言，指質邪正，再被逐，終嬰大禍。

translations.literal: Deyu again invoked Xiang's words, pointing directly at evil versus good; twice he was driven out, and at last suffered great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu again invoked Xiang's words, pointing directly at evil versus good; twice he was driven out, and at last suffered great calamity.

sentences.zh: 嗟乎！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 朋黨之興也，殆哉！

translations.literal: When factions arise—how perilous!
translations.idiomatic: When factions arise—how perilous!

sentences.zh: 根夫主威奪者下陵，聽弗明者賢不肖兩進，進必務勝，而後人人引所私，以所私乘狐疑不斷之隙；

translations.literal: When the root lies in the sovereign's authority being diminished, subordinates encroach upward; when hearing is unclear, the worthy and unworthy both advance; once advanced each must strive to prevail; afterward every man brings forward those he favors, and with his favorites exploits the gap of uncertainty and indecision—
translations.idiomatic: When the root lies in the sovereign's authority being diminished, subordinates encroach upward; when hearing is unclear, the worthy and unworthy both advance; once advanced each must strive to prevail; afterward every man brings forward those he favors, and with his favorites exploits the gap of uncertainty and indecision—

sentences.zh: 是引桀、蹠、孔、顏相哄於前，而以眾寡為勝負矣。

translations.literal: it is to set Jie, Zhi, Confucius, and Yan Hui shouting at one another in the sovereign's presence, and to decide victory by numbers alone.
translations.idiomatic: it is to set Jie, Zhi, Confucius, and Yan Hui shouting at one another in the sovereign's presence, and to decide victory by numbers alone.

sentences.zh: 欲國不亡，得乎？

translations.literal: Can one wish the state not to perish—and expect it?
translations.idiomatic: Can one wish the state not to perish—and expect it?

sentences.zh: 身為名宰相，不能損所憎，顯擠以仇，使比周勢成，根株牽連，賢智播奔，而王室亦衰，寧明有未哲歟？

translations.literal: Though he was a celebrated chief minister, he could not reduce those he hated, but openly drove out others with enmity, letting clique power take shape, roots and branches intertwined, the wise and talented scattered in flight—and the royal house also declined. Could it be that his brilliance had a measure of un-wisdom?
translations.idiomatic: Though he was a celebrated chief minister, he could not reduce those he hated, but openly drove out others with enmity, letting clique power take shape, roots and branches intertwined, the wise and talented scattered in flight—and the royal house also declined. Could it be that his brilliance had a measure of un-wisdom?

sentences.zh: 不然，功烈光明，佐武中興，與姚、宋等矣。

translations.literal: Otherwise, his achievements and glory would have shone bright—he would have aided Wuzong in restoring the dynasty, and stood equal with Yao and Song.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise, his achievements and glory would have shone bright—he would have aided Wuzong in restoring the dynasty, and stood equal with Yao Chong and Song Jing.
